KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.card_maps.doc: /-- There are `nᵐ` maps from an `m`-element set to an `n`-element set: `2³ = 8` from three elements to two. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.card_maps.statement: theorem card_maps (m n : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Fin m → Fin n) = n ^ m

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.imag_not_real.doc: /-- A non-zero multiple of `i` is not real (`i ∉ ℝ`): `ℝ ⊊ ℂ`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.imag_not_real.statement: theorem imag_not_real (y : ℝ) (hy : y ≠ 0) : ¬ ∃ x : ℝ, (x : ℂ) = y * Complex.I

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.glue_eqvGen_i.doc:
/-- On the square `[0, L]²` (`L > 0`), the equivalence relation generated by the gluing identifies two points exactly
when their coordinates agree after `L ↦ 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.glue_eqvGen_i.statement:
theorem glue_eqvGen_iff (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) (p q : ℝ × ℝ) (hp : p ∈ square L) (hq : q ∈ square L) :
    Relation.EqvGen (glue L) p q ↔ κ L p.1 = κ L q.1 ∧ κ L p.2 = κ L q.2

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.coset_space_h.doc: /-- The quotient of `SO(3)` by "same image of `p₀`" is Hausdorff, being homeomorphic to the sphere (`SO(3)/SO(2)`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.coset_space_h.statement: theorem coset_space_hausdorff (p₀ : Fin 3 → ℝ) (hp₀ : p₀ ∈ sphere) : T2Space (Quotient (orbitSetoid p₀))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.x_exp_le.doc:
/-- `x e^{-x} ≤ e^{-1}` for every `x`, with equality at `x = 1`: the maximum on `[0, 2]` (and on `(0, 2)`) is `e^{-1}`,
at `1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.x_exp_le.statement: theorem x_exp_le (x : ℝ) : x * Real.exp (-x) ≤ Real.exp (-1) ∧ 1 * Real.exp (-1) = Real.exp (-1)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.odd_pow_bijec.doc: /-- Odd powers are bijections of `ℝ` (`x³` for `k = 1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.odd_pow_bijec.statement: theorem odd_pow_bijective (k : ℕ) : Function.Bijective (fun x : ℝ => x ^ (2 * k + 1))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.card_surject.doc: /-- There are `n!` surjective maps from an `n`-element set to itself: `3! = 6`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.card_surject.statement:
theorem card_surjections_self (n : ℕ) :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun f : Fin n → Fin n => Function.Surjective f).card = n.factorial

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.stereoInv_ste.doc:
/-- Applying `σ⁻¹` to the projection `(u, v) = (X, Y) t` of a point of the sphere, `t = 1/(1 - Z)`, gives back
`(X, Y, Z)`: `u² + v² + 1 = 2t`, so `σ⁻¹(u, v) = (X, Y, Z)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.stereoInv_ste.statement:
theorem stereoInv_stereo (X Y Z t : ℝ) (hp : X ^ 2 + Y ^ 2 + Z ^ 2 = 1) (ht : (1 - Z) * t = 1) :
    (X * t) ^ 2 + (Y * t) ^ 2 + 1 = 2 * t ∧ ((X * t) ^ 2 + (Y * t) ^ 2 - 1) = Z * (2 * t)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.no_injection.doc:
/-- The pigeonhole principle: no map from an `m`-element set to an `n`-element set with `n < m` is injective (none
from three elements to two). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.no_injection.statement: theorem no_injection (m n : ℕ) (h : n < m) (f : Fin m → Fin n) : ¬ Function.Injective f

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.angle_equiv.doc: /-- Differing by a multiple of `T` is an equivalence relation on `ℝ`: the angles for `T = 2π`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.angle_equiv.statement: theorem angle_equivalence (T : ℝ) : Equivalence (fun x y : ℝ => ∃ k : ℤ, y - x = k * T)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.finite_map_s.doc: /-- `1, 2 ↦ x`, `3 ↦ y` is surjective onto a codomain whose elements are `x` and `y`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.finite_map_s.statement: theorem finite_map_surjective {β : Type} (x y : β) (h : ∀ b, b = x ∨ b = y) : Function.Surjective ![x, x, y]

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.homeomorp.doc: /-- A homeomorphism sends open sets to open sets and closed sets to closed sets. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.homeomorp.statement:
theorem homeomorph_open_closed (X Y : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (f : X ≃ₜ Y) (U : Set X) :
    (IsOpen U → IsOpen (f '' U)) ∧ (IsClosed U → IsClosed (f '' U))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.topolo.doc: /-- The number of topologies on `n` points, for `n ≤ 5`, is `1, 1, 4, 29, 355, 6942`. -/

KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.hausdo.doc: /-- On three points a family is a Hausdorff topology exactly when it is the discrete topology: one of the `29`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.hausdo.statement: theorem hausdorff_three (F : Finset (Finset (Fin 3))) : IsFinTop F ∧ IsHausdorffFin F ↔ F = Finset.univ

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.deriv_cubic.statement: theorem deriv_cubic (x : ℝ) : deriv (fun x : ℝ => x ^ 3 + x) x = 3 * x ^ 2 + 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.stereo_stereo.doc: /-- Projecting `σ⁻¹(u, v)` gives back `(u, v)`: `1 - Z = 2w`, and `X/(1 - Z) = u`, `Y/(1 - Z) = v`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.stereo_stereo.statement:
theorem stereo_stereoInv (u v w : ℝ) (hw : (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 + 1) * w = 1) :
    1 - (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 - 1) * w = 2 * w ∧ (2 * u * w) = u * (2 * w) ∧ (2 * v * w) = v * (2 * w)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.sphere_slice.doc:
/-- The sphere meets the plane `Z = c` (`|c| < 1`) in a circle of radius `√(1 - c²)`, a set with infinitely many
elements: for `c = ½`, the circle `X² + Y² = ¾`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.sphere_slice.statement:
theorem sphere_slice (c : ℝ) (hc : c ^ 2 < 1) :
    sphere ∩ {p | p 2 = c} = {p | p 0 ^ 2 + p 1 ^ 2 = 1 - c ^ 2 ∧ p 2 = c} ∧
      (sphere ∩ {p | p 2 = c}).Infinite

KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.betwee.doc: /-- Every topology on a finite set lies between the indiscrete one `{∅, X}` and the discrete one (all subsets). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.betwee.statement:
theorem between_indiscrete_discrete {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (F : Finset (Finset α))
    (hF : IsFinTop F) : ({∅, Finset.univ} : Finset (Finset α)) ⊆ F ∧ F ⊆ Finset.univ

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.three_bijecti.doc: /-- `1 ↦ x`, `2 ↦ y`, `3 ↦ z` is a bijection onto `{x, y, z}` (distinct labels exhausting the codomain). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.three_bijecti.statement:
theorem three_bijective {β : Type} (x y z : β) (hxy : x ≠ y) (hxz : x ≠ z) (hyz : y ≠ z)
    (h : ∀ b, b = x ∨ b = y ∨ b = z) : Function.Bijective ![x, y, z]

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Exercises.periodic_desc.doc:
/-- A continuous `T`-periodic function on `ℝ` descends to a continuous function on `ℝ/Tℤ`, with `f = f̄ ∘ π` (`cos`
and the circle, `T = 2π`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Exercises.periodic_desc.statement:
theorem periodic_descends_continuous (T : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Continuous f) (hp : Function.Periodic f T) :
    ∃ g : Quotient (angleSetoid T) → ℝ, Continuous g ∧ ∀ x, g (Quotient.mk _ x) = f x

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.card_perm_succ.doc:
/-- The tree of choices: a bijection of `n + 1` elements chooses the value of the first element among `n + 1`, then a
bijection of the remaining `n`: `(n + 1)! = (n + 1) · n!`, so `3! = 3 · 2 · 1 = 6`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.card_perm_succ.statement:
theorem card_perm_succ (n : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (Equiv.Perm (Fin (n + 1))) = (n + 1) * Fintype.card (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.card_le_of_inj.doc: /-- An injective map between finite sets has `|X| ≤ |Y|`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.card_le_of_inj.statement:
theorem card_le_of_injective (X Y : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] (f : X → Y) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card X ≤ Fintype.card Y

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.le_refl_tra.statement: theorem le_refl_trans (a b c : ℤ) : a ≤ a ∧ (a ≤ b → b ≤ c → a ≤ c)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.card_three.doc: /-- A set listed by three distinct elements has three elements (`{1, 2, 3}` among the instances). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.card_three.statement:
theorem card_three {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] (a b c : α) (hab : a ≠ b) (hac : a ≠ c) (hbc : b ≠ c) :
    ({a, b, c} : Finset α).card = 3

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.odd_diff_no.doc: /-- "`a - b` is odd" is not reflexive (`a - a = 0` is even) and not transitive (odd plus odd is even). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.odd_diff_no.statement: theorem odd_diff_not_equivalence (a b c : ℤ) : ¬ Odd (a - a) ∧ (Odd (a - b) → Odd (b - c) → ¬ Odd (a - c))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.quotie.doc:
/-- In `ℝ/Tℤ`: a set of classes is open exactly when its preimage, a `T`-periodic set, is open in `ℝ`; and the
quotient map is open, since the preimage of the image of `U` is the union of the translates `U + kT`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.quotie.statement:
theorem quotient_open_sets (T : ℝ) (V : Set (Quotient (angleSetoid T))) (U : Set ℝ) (hU : IsOpen U) :
    (IsOpen V ↔ IsOpen (Quotient.mk (angleSetoid T) ⁻¹' V)) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ Quotient.mk (angleSetoid T) ⁻¹' V, x + T ∈ Quotient.mk (angleSetoid T) ⁻¹' V) ∧
      Quotient.mk (angleSetoid T) ⁻¹' (Quotient.mk (angleSetoid T) '' U) = ⋃ k : ℤ, (fun x => x + k * T) '' U ∧
      IsOpen (Quotient.mk (angleSetoid T) '' U)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.stereoInv_hei.doc: /-- `σ⁻¹(u, v)` is not the north pole: its height is `1 - 2w < 1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.stereoInv_hei.statement: theorem stereoInv_height (u v w : ℝ) (hw : (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 + 1) * w = 1) : (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 - 1) * w = 1 - 2 * w

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.class_squar.doc: /-- The class of `x` under "same square" is `{x, -x}`, two elements for `x ≠ 0` and one for `x = 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.class_squar.statement: theorem class_square (x : ℝ) : {y : ℝ | y ^ 2 = x ^ 2} = {x, -x} ∧ (x ≠ 0 → x ≠ -x)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.great_circle_.statement:
theorem great_circle_endpoints :
    Real.sin (Real.pi * 0 / 2) = 0 ∧ Real.cos (Real.pi * 0 / 2) = 1 ∧ Real.sin (Real.pi * 1 / 2) = 1 ∧
      Real.cos (Real.pi * 1 / 2) = 0

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.zmod_prime_fie.doc: /-- `ℤ_p` is a field for `p` prime (`ℤ₂`, `ℤ₃`, `ℤ₅`): every non-zero class has a multiplicative inverse. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.zmod_prime_fie.statement: theorem zmod_prime_field (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : ∀ a : ZMod p, a ≠ 0 → ∃ b : ZMod p, a * b = 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.transition_.doc:
/-- The transition map `x_S ∘ x_N⁻¹` of the stereographic charts from the north and south poles is the inversion
`(u, v) ↦ (u, v)/(u² + v²)`: with `(X, Y, Z) = x_N⁻¹(u, v) = (2u, 2v, u² + v² - 1) d`, `X = u w (1 + Z)` and
`Y = v w (1 + Z)`, that is `x_S = (X, Y)/(1 + Z) = (u w, v w)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.transition_.statement:
theorem transition_inversion (u v w d : ℝ) (hw : (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2) * w = 1) (hd : (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 + 1) * d = 1) :
    2 * u * d = u * w * (1 + (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 - 1) * d) ∧ 2 * v * d = v * w * (1 + (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 - 1) * d)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.mem_circle_sphere.doc: /-- The circle and the sphere are cut out by one equation each (membership is the equation). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.mem_circle_sphere.statement:
theorem mem_circle_sphere (X Y Z : ℝ) :
    ((X, Y) ∈ circle ↔ X ^ 2 + Y ^ 2 = 1) ∧ (![X, Y, Z] ∈ sphere ↔ X ^ 2 + Y ^ 2 + Z ^ 2 = 1)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.t1_thr.doc:
/-- On three points a topology in which every point is closed (the complement of each point open) is the discrete one,
as for the Hausdorff condition. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.t1_thr.statement:
theorem t1_three (F : Finset (Finset (Fin 3))) :
    IsFinTop F ∧ (∀ x : Fin 3, ({x}ᶜ : Finset (Fin 3)) ∈ F) ↔ F = Finset.univ

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.floor_discon.doc:
/-- The preimage of `(k - ½, k + ½)` under the floor function is `[k, k + 1)`, not open; the floor function is
discontinuous at every integer `k` and continuous on `(k, k + 1)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.floor_discon.statement:
theorem floor_discontinuity (k : ℤ) :
    (fun x : ℝ => (⌊x⌋ : ℝ)) ⁻¹' Ioo (k - 1 / 2) (k + 1 / 2) = Ico (k : ℝ) (k + 1) ∧
      ¬ ContinuousAt (fun x : ℝ => (⌊x⌋ : ℝ)) k ∧ ContinuousOn (fun x : ℝ => (⌊x⌋ : ℝ)) (Ioo (k : ℝ) (k + 1))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.hausdorff_con.doc: /-- In a Hausdorff space limits are unique and single points are closed. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.hausdorff_con.statement:
theorem hausdorff_consequences (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] (u : ℕ → X) (a b : X)
    (ha : Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 a)) (hb : Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 b)) : a = b ∧ IsClosed ({a} : Set X)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.deriv_x_exp.statement: theorem deriv_x_exp (x : ℝ) : deriv (fun x : ℝ => x * Real.exp (-x)) x = (1 - x) * Real.exp (-x)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.double_not_surj.doc: /-- Doubling on `ℤ₆` is not surjective: some element is no double (Sage finds `1`, outside the image `{0, 2, 4}`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.double_not_surj.statement: theorem double_not_surjective : ∃ y : ZMod 6, ∀ k : ZMod 6, 2 * k ≠ y

KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.hausdo.doc: /-- On two points a family is a Hausdorff topology exactly when it is the discrete topology: one of the `4`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.hausdo.statement: theorem hausdorff_two (F : Finset (Finset (Fin 2))) : IsFinTop F ∧ IsHausdorffFin F ↔ F = Finset.univ

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.prodMap_inject.doc:
/-- For non-empty sets, `f × g` is injective exactly when `f` and `g` are, and surjective exactly when `f` and `g`
are. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.prodMap_inject.statement:
theorem prodMap_injective_surjective {X X' Y Y' : Type} [Nonempty X] [Nonempty Y] [Nonempty X'] [Nonempty Y']
    (f : X → X') (g : Y → Y') :
    (Function.Injective (Prod.map f g) ↔ Function.Injective f ∧ Function.Injective g) ∧
      (Function.Surjective (Prod.map f g) ↔ Function.Surjective f ∧ Function.Surjective g)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.cos_half_anti.doc: /-- `cos(φ/2)` changes sign under `φ ↦ φ + 2π`, so it does not descend. -/

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.le_not_symm.statement: theorem le_not_symm : ∃ a b : ℤ, 1 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 4 ∧ 1 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 4 ∧ a ≤ b ∧ ¬ b ≤ a

KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.infinite_inter.doc:
/-- The intervals `(-c/(n + 1), c/(n + 1))` (`c > 0`) intersect in `{0}`, which is not open: an infinite intersection
of open sets need not be open (`c = 1`: the intervals `(-1/n, 1/n)`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.infinite_inter.statement:
theorem infinite_inter_not_open (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    (⋂ n : ℕ, Ioo (-c / (n + 1)) (c / (n + 1))) = {0} ∧ ¬ IsOpen ({0} : Set ℝ)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.zmod5_inverses.statement: theorem zmod5_inverses : ∃ b₁ b₂ b₃ b₄ : ZMod 5, 1 * b₁ = 1 ∧ 2 * b₂ = 1 ∧ 3 * b₃ = 1 ∧ 4 * b₄ = 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.inversion_i.doc: /-- The inversion is its own inverse: `|(u w, v w)|² = w`, and `(u w, v w)/w = (u, v)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.inversion_i.statement:
theorem inversion_involutive (u v w : ℝ) (hw : (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2) * w = 1) :
    (u * w) ^ 2 + (v * w) ^ 2 = w

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.descends_iff_.doc:
/-- A function descends to `ℝ/Tℤ` (is constant on the classes of "differ by a multiple of `T`") exactly when it is
`T`-periodic: `cos` and `sin` descend to the circle. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.descends_iff_.statement:
theorem descends_iff_periodic {Y : Type} (T : ℝ) (f : ℝ → Y) :
    (∀ x y, (∃ k : ℤ, y - x = k * T) → f x = f y) ↔ Function.Periodic f T

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.Ico_not_h.doc:
/-- `[a, b)` and `(c, d)` are not homeomorphic: removing `a` leaves the connected `(a, b)`, while removing any point
`f(a)` from `(c, d)` leaves two pieces (`[0, 1)` and `(0, 1)`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.Ico_not_h.statement: theorem Ico_not_homeomorph_Ioo (a b c d : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (hcd : c < d) : IsEmpty (Ico a b ≃ₜ Ioo c d)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.cubic_three_r.doc: /-- `g(x) = x³ - x` has three distinct roots (Sage finds `-1, 0, 1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.cubic_three_r.statement: theorem cubic_three_roots : ∃ x y z : ℝ, x < y ∧ y < z ∧ x ^ 3 - x = 0 ∧ y ^ 3 - y = 0 ∧ z ^ 3 - z = 0

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.class_cos.doc: /-- The class of `x` under "same cosine" is `{±x + 2πk}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.class_cos.statement:
theorem class_cos (x : ℝ) : {y : ℝ | Real.cos y = Real.cos x} = {y | ∃ k : ℤ, y = x + k * (2 * Real.pi) ∨
    y = -x + k * (2 * Real.pi)}

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.matrix_maps_.doc:
/-- Matrix multiplication, the determinant and `g ↦ g · v` are continuous (each entry is a polynomial in the
entries); `v = (0, 0, 1)` gives the orbit map. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.matrix_maps_.statement:
theorem matrix_maps_continuous (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → ℝ) :
    Continuous (fun p : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ => p.1 * p.2) ∧
      Continuous (fun g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ => g.det) ∧
      Continuous (fun g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ => g *ᵥ v)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.sameValue_e.doc:
/-- For any map `f`, "same value under `f`" is an equivalence relation (for the orbit map on `SO(3)`, "same image of
the north pole"). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.sameValue_e.statement: theorem sameValue_equivalence {X Y : Type} (f : X → Y) : Equivalence (fun x x' => f x = f x')

KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.parabola_hyper.doc:
/-- The region `v > u² + c` above a parabola is open; the hyperbola `uv = c` is closed; `ℝ² ∖ {p}` is open (for
`c = 0`, `c = 1` and `p = 0`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.parabola_hyper.statement:
theorem parabola_hyperbola (c : ℝ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) :
    IsOpen {q : ℝ × ℝ | q.2 > q.1 ^ 2 + c} ∧ IsClosed {q : ℝ × ℝ | q.1 * q.2 = c} ∧ IsOpen ({p}ᶜ : Set (ℝ × ℝ))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.stereoInv_sph.statement:
theorem stereoInv_sphere (u v w : ℝ) (hw : (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 + 1) * w = 1) :
    (2 * u * w) ^ 2 + (2 * v * w) ^ 2 + ((u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 - 1) * w) ^ 2 = 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.card_prod.doc: /-- A product of finite sets has `|X| · |Y|` elements (`2 · 3 = 6` pairs, `2 · 3 · 2 = 12` triples). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.card_prod.statement: theorem card_prod (X Y : Type) [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] : Fintype.card (X × Y) = Fintype.card X * Fintype.card Y

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.segment_joine.doc: /-- Any two points of `ℝⁿ` are joined by the straight segment `γ(t) = (1 - t) p + t q`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.segment_joine.statement: theorem segment_joined (n : ℕ) (p q : Fin n → ℝ) : JoinedIn univ p q

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.close_not_t.statement:
theorem close_not_trans : ∃ a b c : ℤ, 1 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 4 ∧ 1 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 4 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 ∧
    |a - b| ≤ 1 ∧ |b - c| ≤ 1 ∧ ¬ |a - c| ≤ 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.two_hausdorff.doc:
/-- On `ℝⁿ` (`n ≥ 1`) the usual topology and the discrete one are both Hausdorff, and they differ (the usual one
is not discrete). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.two_hausdorff.statement:
theorem two_hausdorff_topologies (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    T2Space (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) ∧ @T2Space (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) ⊥ ∧
      ¬ DiscreteTopology (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.union_inter_op.doc: /-- Any union of open sets of `ℝⁿ` is open, and any finite intersection is open. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.union_inter_op.statement:
theorem union_inter_open (n : ℕ) (S : Set (Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))) (hS : ∀ U ∈ S, IsOpen U)
    (F : Finset (Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))) (hF : ∀ U ∈ F, IsOpen U) :
    IsOpen (⋃₀ S) ∧ IsOpen (⋂₀ (F : Set (Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.topolo.doc:
/-- The topologies on three points: Sage lists `29` families, without repetition, and they are exactly the families
satisfying the axioms. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.topolo.statement:
theorem topologies_three : ∃ L : List (Finset (Finset (Fin 3))), L.Nodup ∧ L.length = 29 ∧
    ∀ F : Finset (Finset (Fin 3)), F ∈ L ↔ IsFinTop F

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.sq_not_inject.doc: /-- `x ↦ x²` is not injective: two distinct arguments with the same square (Sage finds `(-1)² = 1²`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.sq_not_inject.statement: theorem sq_not_injective : ∃ x y : ℝ, x ≠ y ∧ x ^ 2 = y ^ 2

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.height_preimage_em.doc: /-- `|Z| ≤ 1` on the sphere, so `h⁻¹([a, b])` is empty for `1 < a`: `h⁻¹([2, 3]) = ∅`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.height_preimage_em.statement: theorem height_preimage_empty (a b : ℝ) (ha : 1 < a) : sphere ∩ height ⁻¹' Set.Icc a b = ∅

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.close_refl_.statement: theorem close_refl_symm (a b : ℤ) : |a - a| ≤ 1 ∧ (|a - b| ≤ 1 → |b - a| ≤ 1)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.union.doc:
/-- On two points the union of two topologies is again a topology (the union of the two Sierpiński topologies is the
discrete one). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.union.statement: theorem union_two_points (F G : Finset (Finset (Fin 2))) (hF : IsFinTop F) (hG : IsFinTop G) : IsFinTop (F ∪ G)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.comp_assoc.doc: /-- Composition is associative: `(h ∘ g) ∘ f = h ∘ (g ∘ f)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.comp_assoc.statement: theorem comp_assoc {W X Y Z : Type} (f : W → X) (g : X → Y) (h : Y → Z) : (h ∘ g) ∘ f = h ∘ (g ∘ f)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.disjoint_ball.doc: /-- Two distinct points of `ℝⁿ` at distance `d` have disjoint balls of radius `d/2`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.disjoint_ball.statement:
theorem disjoint_balls (n : ℕ) (x y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
    Disjoint (ball x (dist x y / 2)) (ball y (dist x y / 2))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.torus_point_r4.doc: /-- The point of `S¹ × S¹ ⊂ ℝ⁴` with angles `(π/3, π/2)` is `(½, √3/2, 0, 1)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.torus_point_r4.statement:
theorem torus_point_r4 :
    Real.cos (Real.pi / 3) = 1 / 2 ∧ Real.sin (Real.pi / 3) = Real.sqrt 3 / 2 ∧ Real.cos (Real.pi / 2) = 0 ∧
      Real.sin (Real.pi / 2) = 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.rn_succ_prod.doc: /-- `ℝⁿ⁺¹ = ℝ × ℝⁿ`: a list of `n + 1` numbers is its first number and the list of the others. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.rn_succ_prod.statement: theorem rn_succ_prod (n : ℕ) : Function.Bijective (fun x : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ => (x 0, Fin.tail x))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.compl.doc: /-- `{∅, A, Aᶜ, X}` is a topology for any subset `A`: `{∅, {1}, {2, 3}, X}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.compl.statement:
theorem complement_pair_isFinTop {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (A : Finset α) :
    IsFinTop ({∅, A, Aᶜ, Finset.univ} : Finset (Finset α))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.pair_injectiv.doc: /-- `1 ↦ x`, `2 ↦ y` is injective when `x ≠ y`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.pair_injectiv.statement: theorem pair_injective {β : Type} (x y : β) (hxy : x ≠ y) : Function.Injective ![x, y]

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.infinite_of_charZe.doc: /-- A ring of characteristic zero (`ℤ`, `ℝ`, `ℂ`) is infinite. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.infinite_of_charZe.statement: theorem infinite_of_charZero (K : Type) [AddMonoidWithOne K] [CharZero K] : Infinite K

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.wrap_Ico_.doc:
/-- `φ ↦ (cos φ, sin φ)` is a continuous bijection from `[a, a + 2π)` onto the circle, but it has no continuous
inverse: a continuous `g` with `g(cos φ, sin φ) = φ` on `[a, a + 2π)` would give `g(wrap a) = a + 2π` by continuity
(`a = 0`: the inverse jumps at `(1, 0)`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.wrap_Ico_.statement:
theorem wrap_Ico_not_homeomorph (a : ℝ) :
    BijOn wrap (Ico a (a + 2 * Real.pi)) circle ∧
      ¬ ∃ g : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ, ContinuousOn g circle ∧ ∀ φ ∈ Ico a (a + 2 * Real.pi), g (wrap φ) = φ

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.wrap_preimage.doc:
/-- The preimage of the point `(cos a, sin a)` under `φ ↦ (cos φ, sin φ)` is `a + 2πℤ`: for `(1, 0)` (`a = 0`), the
multiples of `2π`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.wrap_preimage.statement: theorem wrap_preimage (a : ℝ) : wrap ⁻¹' {wrap a} = {φ | ∃ k : ℤ, φ = a + k * (2 * Real.pi)}

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.upper_part_ope.doc:
/-- The part `{Y > t}` of the circle is open in the circle (the trace of an open half-plane): the open upper half for
`t = 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.upper_part_ope.statement: theorem upper_part_open (t : ℝ) : IsOpen ((Subtype.val : circle → ℝ × ℝ) ⁻¹' {p | t < p.2})

KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.rectangle_open.doc:
/-- Open rectangles `(a, b) × (c, d)` are open in `ℝ²` (the domain `(0, π) × (0, 2π)` of spherical coordinates), and
`ℝ²` itself is open. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.rectangle_open.statement: theorem rectangle_open (a b c d : ℝ) : IsOpen (Ioo a b ×ˢ Ioo c d) ∧ IsOpen (univ : Set (ℝ × ℝ))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.x_exp_no_min.doc:
/-- On `(0, 2)`, `f > 0` and no value is a minimum: below every value there is a smaller one, and the infimum `0` is
not attained. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.x_exp_no_min.statement:
theorem x_exp_no_min (x : ℝ) (hx : x ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 2) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    0 < x * Real.exp (-x) ∧ (∃ y ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 2, y * Real.exp (-y) < x * Real.exp (-x)) ∧
      ∃ y ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 2, y * Real.exp (-y) < ε

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.heine_borel.doc: /-- Heine-Borel: a subset of a proper metric space such as `ℝⁿ` is compact exactly when it is closed and bounded. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.heine_borel.statement:
theorem heine_borel (E : Type) [MetricSpace E] [ProperSpace E] (K : Set E) :
    IsCompact K ↔ IsClosed K ∧ Bornology.IsBounded K

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.card_eq_of_bi.doc: /-- Finite sets related by a bijection have the same number of elements. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.card_eq_of_bi.statement:
theorem card_eq_of_bijective {X Y : Type} [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] (f : X → Y) (hf : Function.Bijective f) :
    Fintype.card X = Fintype.card Y

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.surjective_i.doc: /-- A map is surjective exactly when its image is the whole codomain. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.surjective_i.statement: theorem surjective_iff_range {X Y : Type} (f : X → Y) : Function.Surjective f ↔ Set.range f = Set.univ

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.doubles_subset.statement: theorem doubles_subset (n : ℕ) : (Finset.range n).image (2 * ·) ⊆ Finset.range (2 * n)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.card_fun.doc: /-- The maps between finite sets `X → Y` number `|Y|^|X|`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.card_fun.statement:
theorem card_fun (X Y : Type) [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] :
    Fintype.card (X → Y) = Fintype.card Y ^ Fintype.card X

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.classes_par.doc:
/-- The classes of an equivalence relation partition the set: two classes are equal or disjoint, and every element
lies in its own class, hence in exactly one. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.classes_par.statement:
theorem classes_partition {X : Type} (s : Setoid X) (x y : X) :
    ({z | s z x} = {z | s z y} ∨ Disjoint {z | s z x} {z | s z y}) ∧ x ∈ {z | s z x} ∧
      (∀ w, x ∈ {z | s z w} → {z | s z w} = {z | s z x})

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.sq_preimage_neg.doc: /-- No square is negative: the preimage of `{y}` under `x ↦ x²` is empty for `y < 0` (`y = -1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.sq_preimage_neg.statement: theorem sq_preimage_neg (y : ℝ) (hy : y < 0) : (fun x : ℝ => x ^ 2) ⁻¹' {y} = ∅

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.class_mod.statement:
theorem class_mod (n m r : ℕ) (hr : r < n) :
    (Finset.range (n * m)).filter (fun k => k % n = r) = (Finset.range m).image (fun j => r + n * j)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.exp_I_periodi.doc: /-- `e^{iφ}` is `2π`-periodic and descends to the circle. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.exp_I_periodi.statement: theorem exp_I_periodic (φ : ℝ) : Complex.exp ((φ + 2 * Real.pi : ℝ) * Complex.I) = Complex.exp (φ * Complex.I)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.subspace_haus.doc: /-- Every subspace of a Hausdorff space is Hausdorff: the circle, the sphere, the torus and `SO(3)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.subspace_haus.statement: theorem subspace_hausdorff (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] (S : Set X) : T2Space S

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.O2_components.doc:
/-- `O(2)` has exactly two components, the rotations and the reflections, each a circle: the component of `g` is the
set of orthogonal matrices with the determinant of `g`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.O2_components.statement:
theorem O2_components (g : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ) (hg : g ∈ O2) :
    connectedComponentIn O2 g = {h ∈ O2 | h.det = g.det}

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.z12_to_z4.doc: /-- `k mod 12 ↦ k mod 4` is a surjection `ℤ₁₂ → ℤ₄` whose preimages have three elements each. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.z12_to_z4.statement:
theorem z12_to_z4 (y : ZMod 4) :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun x : ZMod 12 => ZMod.castHom (by norm_num : 4 ∣ 12) (ZMod 4) x = y).card = 3

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.affine_soluti.statement: theorem affine_solution_check (y w : ℝ) (hw : 2 * w = 1) : 2 * ((y - 1) * w) + 1 = y

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.cos_half_chan.doc:
/-- Wherever `cos(φ/2) ≠ 0`, the values at `φ` and `φ + 2π` differ: `cos(φ/2)` is not constant on classes (at
`φ = 0` it changes from `1` to `-1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.cos_half_chan.statement: theorem cos_half_changes (φ : ℝ) (h : Real.cos (φ / 2) ≠ 0) : Real.cos ((φ + 2 * Real.pi) / 2) ≠ Real.cos (φ / 2)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.moebiu.doc:
/-- The boundary of the Möbius band is a single circle: the image of the top and bottom edges is connected (the half
twist joins the top edge to the bottom one). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.moebiu.statement:
theorem moebius_boundary_connected (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) :
    IsConnected (Quotient.mk (edgeSetoid L true) '' topBottom L)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.maps_three_as_.doc: /-- A map `{1, 2, 3} → Y` is the triple of its values: `f ↦ (f 1, f 2, f 3)` is a bijection onto `Y × Y × Y`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.maps_three_as_.statement:
theorem maps_three_as_triples (β : Type) :
    Function.Bijective (fun f : Fin 3 → β => (f 0, f 1, f 2))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.Rz_transpose_mu.statement: theorem Rz_transpose_mul (α : ℝ) : (Rz α)ᵀ * Rz α = 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.int_real_complex_i.doc:
/-- `ℤ ⊆ ℝ ⊆ ℂ`: the inclusions are injective (distinct integers are distinct reals, distinct reals distinct complex
numbers). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.int_real_complex_i.statement:
theorem int_real_complex_inclusions (a b : ℤ) (x y : ℝ) :
    ((a : ℝ) = b → a = b) ∧ ((x : ℂ) = y → x = y)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.sph_injOn.doc: /-- Spherical coordinates are injective on `(0, π) × (a, a + 2π)`: on `(0, π) × (0, 2π)` for `a = 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.sph_injOn.statement:
theorem sph_injOn (a : ℝ) :
    Set.InjOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => sph q.1 q.2) (Set.Ioo 0 Real.pi ×ˢ Set.Ioo a (a + 2 * Real.pi))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.quotie.doc: /-- A map out of a quotient is continuous exactly when its composition with the quotient map is. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.quotie.statement:
theorem quotient_continuous_iff (X Y : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (s : Setoid X)
    (g : Quotient s → Y) : Continuous g ↔ Continuous (g ∘ Quotient.mk s)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.interv.doc:
/-- `[0, L]` with `0 ∼ L` (`L > 0`) is homeomorphic to the circle by `[φ] ↦ (cos(2πφ/L), sin(2πφ/L))` (for `L = 2π`,
`[φ] ↦ (cos φ, sin φ)`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.interv.statement:
theorem interval_quotient_homeomorph (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) :
    ∃ e : Quotient (intervalSetoid L) ≃ₜ circle, ∀ p : Icc (0 : ℝ) L, (e ⟦p⟧ : ℝ × ℝ) =
      wrap (2 * Real.pi * p.1 / L)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.range_wrap.doc: /-- `φ ↦ (r cos φ, r sin φ)` (`r ≥ 0`) has image the circle `X² + Y² = r²`: for `r = 1`, the circle `S¹`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.range_wrap.statement:
theorem range_wrap (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) :
    Set.range (fun φ => (r * Real.cos φ, r * Real.sin φ)) = {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.1 ^ 2 + p.2 ^ 2 = r ^ 2}

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.orbit_image.doc:
/-- The orbit map sends `SO(3)` onto the sphere: a point is on the sphere exactly when some rotation moves the north
pole to it. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.orbit_image.statement: theorem orbit_image (p : Fin 3 → ℝ) : p ∈ sphere ↔ ∃ g ∈ SO3, orbit g = p

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.inter.doc: /-- The common open sets of two topologies form a topology. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.inter.statement:
theorem inter_isTopologyOn (X : Type) (O₁ O₂ : Set (Set X)) (h₁ : IsTopologyOn X O₁) (h₂ : IsTopologyOn X O₂) :
    IsTopologyOn X (O₁ ∩ O₂)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.subspace_trans.doc:
/-- For `Z ⊆ Y ⊆ X`, the topology `Z` inherits from the subspace `Y` (through the inclusion `Z → Y`) is the one it
inherits from `X` directly. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.subspace_trans.statement:
theorem subspace_transitive (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (Y Z : Set X) (h : Z ⊆ Y) :
    TopologicalSpace.induced (Set.inclusion h) (inferInstance : TopologicalSpace Y) =
      (inferInstance : TopologicalSpace Z)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.height_cap.doc:
/-- On the sphere, `h⁻¹((c, 1]) = {Z > c}` (since `Z ≤ 1`), and it contains the north pole for `c < 1`: the open cap
above `Z = ½`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.height_cap.statement:
theorem height_cap (c : ℝ) (hc : c < 1) :
    sphere ∩ height ⁻¹' Set.Ioc c 1 = sphere ∩ {p | c < p 2} ∧ northPole ∈ sphere ∩ height ⁻¹' Set.Ioc c 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.rotation_cur.doc: /-- For a continuous family of rotations `R(t)`, `t ↦ R(t) · (0, 0, 1)` is a continuous curve on the sphere. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.rotation_cur.statement:
theorem rotation_curve (R : ℝ → Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) (hR : Continuous R) (hSO : ∀ t, R t ∈ SO3) :
    Continuous (fun t => orbit (R t)) ∧ ∀ t, orbit (R t) ∈ sphere

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.edge_interior.doc:
/-- A point `(0, v)` of `[0, 1]²` with `0 < v < 1` is identified exactly with `(1, v)` (a two-element class), and an
interior point `(u, v)` is alone in its class. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.edge_interior.statement:
theorem edge_interior_classes (v : ℝ) (hv : v ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (q : ℝ × ℝ) (hq : q ∈ square 1) :
    (Relation.EqvGen (glue 1) (0, v) q ↔ q = (0, v) ∨ q = (1, v)) ∧
      (∀ u ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, Relation.EqvGen (glue 1) (u, v) q ↔ q = (u, v))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.range_mul_cos.doc: /-- `x ↦ a cos x` (`a ≥ 0`) has image `[-a, a]`: `cos` has image `[-1, 1]`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.range_mul_cos.statement: theorem range_mul_cos (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : Set.range (fun x => a * Real.cos x) = Set.Icc (-a) a

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.shift_inverse.doc:
/-- The shift `k ↦ k + a` of `ℤₙ` is undone by `k ↦ k - a` in both orders, so it is a bijection: `k ↦ k + 1` on
`ℤ₆`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.shift_inverse.statement:
theorem shift_inverse (n : ℕ) (a : ZMod n) :
    Function.LeftInverse (fun k => k - a) (fun k => k + a) ∧ Function.RightInverse (fun k => k - a) (fun k => k + a) ∧
      Function.Bijective (fun k : ZMod n => k + a)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.bijective_iff_h.doc: /-- A map is a bijection exactly when it has an inverse `g`, with `g (f x) = x` and `f (g y) = y`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.bijective_iff_h.statement:
theorem bijective_iff_has_inverse {X Y : Type} (f : X → Y) :
    Function.Bijective f ↔ ∃ g : Y → X, Function.LeftInverse g f ∧ Function.RightInverse g f

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.ball_.doc: /-- The open sets of `ℝⁿ` (sets containing a ball around each of their points) form a topology. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.ball_.statement:
theorem ball_opens_topology (n : ℕ) :
    IsTopologyOn (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) {V | ∀ x ∈ V, ∃ ε > 0, ball x ε ⊆ V}

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.mul_tan_bijOn.doc: /-- `x ↦ a tan x` (`a ≠ 0`) is a bijection of `(-π/2, π/2)` onto `ℝ`: `tan` for `a = 1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.mul_tan_bijOn.statement:
theorem mul_tan_bijOn (a : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    Set.BijOn (fun x => a * Real.tan x) (Set.Ioo (-(Real.pi / 2)) (Real.pi / 2)) Set.univ

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.torus_pairs_of.doc:
/-- The torus `S¹ × S¹` (radii `r₁`, `r₂ ≥ 0`) is the set of pairs of points of the two circles, each labelled by
an angle: a point of the torus is labelled by a pair of angles. -/

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.compact_of_clos.doc: /-- A closed and bounded subset of a proper metric space is compact: the circle, the sphere, the torus and `SO(3)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.compact_of_clos.statement:
theorem compact_of_closed_bounded (E : Type) [MetricSpace E] [ProperSpace E] (K : Set E) (hc : IsClosed K)
    (hb : Bornology.IsBounded K) : IsCompact K

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.wrap_periodic.doc: /-- `φ` and `φ + 2π` give the same point, so the parametrisation is not injective on `ℝ`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.wrap_periodic.statement: theorem wrap_periodic (φ : ℝ) : wrap (φ + 2 * Real.pi) = wrap φ

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.cycle_minus_t.doc: /-- The six-cycle minus two opposite vertices splits into the two components `{1, 2}` and `{4, 5}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.cycle_minus_t.statement:
theorem cycle_minus_two (u v : Fin 6) (hu : u ≠ 0 ∧ u ≠ 3) (hv : v ≠ 0 ∧ v ≠ 3) :
    cycleMinusTwo.Reachable u v ↔ (u.val < 3 ↔ v.val < 3)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.finite_map_four.statement:
theorem finite_map_four {β : Type} (a b c : β) (hab : a ≠ b) (hac : a ≠ c) (hbc : b ≠ c) :
    Set.range ![a, c, a, a] = {a, c} ∧ ![a, c, a, a] ⁻¹' {a} = {0, 2, 3} ∧ ![a, c, a, a] ⁻¹' {b} = ∅ ∧
      ![a, c, a, a] ⁻¹' {a, c} = Set.univ

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.great_circle_.doc: /-- `γ(t) = (sin(πt/2), 0, cos(πt/2))` stays on the sphere: `sin² + 0² + cos² = 1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.great_circle_.statement:
theorem great_circle_on_sphere (t : ℝ) :
    Real.sin (Real.pi * t / 2) ^ 2 + 0 ^ 2 + Real.cos (Real.pi * t / 2) ^ 2 = 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.sphere_joined.doc: /-- Any two points of the sphere are joined by a path in the sphere (an arc of a great circle). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.sphere_joined.statement:
theorem sphere_joined (p q : Fin 3 → ℝ) (hp : p ∈ KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.sphere)
    (hq : q ∈ KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.sphere) : JoinedIn KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.sphere p q

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.closed_subset_c.doc: /-- A closed subset of a compact set is compact: the circle, closed in the compact closed disc. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.closed_subset_c.statement:
theorem closed_subset_compact (E : Type) [TopologicalSpace E] (K C : Set E) (hK : IsCompact K) (hC : IsClosed C)
    (hCK : C ⊆ K) : IsCompact C

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.cos_preimage.doc:
/-- For `0 < δ ≤ π`, the preimage of `(cos δ, 2)` under `cos` is the union of the open intervals
`(-δ + 2πk, δ + 2πk)`: for `δ = π/3`, the preimage of `(½, 2)` is `⋃ (-π/3 + 2πk, π/3 + 2πk)`, open. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.cos_preimage.statement:
theorem cos_preimage (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδπ : δ ≤ Real.pi) :
    Real.cos ⁻¹' Ioo (Real.cos δ) 2 = ⋃ k : ℤ, Ioo (-δ + k * (2 * Real.pi)) (δ + k * (2 * Real.pi)) ∧
      IsOpen (Real.cos ⁻¹' Ioo (Real.cos δ) 2)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.sq_preimage_Icc.doc:
/-- For `0 ≤ a ≤ b`, the preimage of `[a², b²]` under `x ↦ x²` is `[-b, -a] ∪ [a, b]`: `[-2, -1] ∪ [1, 2]` for
`[1, 4]`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.sq_preimage_Icc.statement:
theorem sq_preimage_Icc (a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) :
    (fun x : ℝ => x ^ 2) ⁻¹' Set.Icc (a ^ 2) (b ^ 2) = Set.Icc (-b) (-a) ∪ Set.Icc a b

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.connected_ima.doc:
/-- The image of a connected space under a continuous map is connected; for `f : [0, 1] → ℝ` continuous this gives the
intermediate value theorem; and the connected subsets of `ℝ` are the intervals. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.connected_ima.statement:
theorem connected_image_ivt (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc 0 1)) (y : ℝ) (hy : y ∈ Icc (f 0) (f 1)) :
    IsConnected (f '' Icc 0 1) ∧ (∃ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, f x = y) ∧ (f '' Icc 0 1).OrdConnected

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Exercises.circle_quotie.doc: /-- `ℝ/Tℤ` (`T > 0`) with the quotient topology is compact and Hausdorff, although `ℝ` is not compact (`T = 2π`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Exercises.circle_quotie.statement:
theorem circle_quotient_compact_hausdorff (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    CompactSpace (Quotient (angleSetoid T)) ∧ T2Space (Quotient (angleSetoid T)) ∧ ¬ CompactSpace ℝ

KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.Ioc_neither.doc: /-- `(a, b]` (`a < b`) is neither open nor closed: `(1, 2]`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.Ioc_neither.statement: theorem Ioc_neither (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) : ¬ IsOpen (Ioc a b) ∧ ¬ IsClosed (Ioc a b)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.cycle_minus_o.doc: /-- The six-cycle minus one vertex stays connected: any two remaining vertices are joined. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.cycle_minus_o.statement: theorem cycle_minus_one (u v : Fin 6) (hu : u ≠ 5) (hv : v ≠ 5) : cycleMinusOne.Reachable u v

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.log_exp_inverse.statement: theorem log_exp_inverse (x y : ℝ) (hy : 0 < y) : Real.log (Real.exp x) = x ∧ Real.exp (Real.log y) = y

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.x_exp_nonneg.statement: theorem x_exp_nonneg (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x) : 0 ≤ x * Real.exp (-x) ∧ 0 * Real.exp (-0) = (0 : ℝ)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.cubic_not_inj.doc: /-- `g(x) = x³ - x` is not injective: two distinct arguments with the same value. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.cubic_not_inj.statement: theorem cubic_not_injective : ∃ x y : ℝ, x ≠ y ∧ x ^ 3 - x = y ^ 3 - y

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.graph_connect.doc: /-- A graph is connected exactly when it has a vertex and every pair of vertices is joined by a walk. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.graph_connect.statement: theorem graph_connected_iff (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : G.Connected ↔ Nonempty (Fin n) ∧ ∀ u v, G.Reachable u v

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.card_surject.doc:
/-- Of the `2ᵐ` maps from an `m`-element set (`m ≥ 1`) to a two-element set, all but the two constant maps are
surjective: `8 - 2 = 6` for `m = 3`, `16 - 2 = 14` for `m = 4`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.card_surject.statement:
theorem card_surjections_two (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) :
    (Finset.univ.filter fun f : Fin m → Fin 2 => Function.Surjective f).card = 2 ^ m - 2

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.three_maps_in.doc: /-- With distinct labels `a, b, c, d`: `(a, b, c)` and `(d, c, b)` are injective, `(a, a, b)` is not. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.three_maps_in.statement:
theorem three_maps_injectivity {β : Type} [DecidableEq β] (a b c d : β) (hab : a ≠ b) (hac : a ≠ c) (had : a ≠ d)
    (hbc : b ≠ c) (hbd : b ≠ d) (hcd : c ≠ d) :
    Function.Injective ![a, b, c] ∧ ¬ Function.Injective ![a, a, b] ∧ Function.Injective ![d, c, b]

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.wrap_injOn.doc: /-- `φ ↦ (cos φ, sin φ)` is injective on every open interval `(a, a + 2π)` of length `2π`: on `(0, 2π)` for `a = 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.wrap_injOn.statement: theorem wrap_injOn (a : ℝ) : Set.InjOn wrap (Set.Ioo a (a + 2 * Real.pi))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.neg_congrue.doc:
/-- `x` and `-x` lie in the same class modulo `2π` exactly when `x ∈ πℤ`: so a class of "same cosine" has two
elements per period except for `x ∈ πℤ`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.neg_congrue.statement: theorem neg_congruent_iff (x : ℝ) : (∃ k : ℤ, -x = x + k * (2 * Real.pi)) ↔ ∃ m : ℤ, x = m * Real.pi

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.Rz_neg_eq_trans.doc: /-- `R_z(-α) = R_z(α)ᵀ`: the inverse of a rotation is its transpose. -/

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.arctan_tan_inve.statement:
theorem arctan_tan_inverse (x y : ℝ) (hx : x ∈ Set.Ioo (-(Real.pi / 2)) (Real.pi / 2)) :
    Real.arctan (Real.tan x) = x ∧ Real.tan (Real.arctan y) = y

KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.ball_radius_su.doc: /-- Around `x ∈ B_ε(p)` the ball of radius `δ = ε - |x - p|` lies in `B_ε(p)`, so open balls are open. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.ball_radius_su.statement:
theorem ball_radius_subset (n : ℕ) (p x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (ε : ℝ) (hx : x ∈ ball p ε) :
    0 < ε - dist x p ∧ ball x (ε - dist x p) ⊆ ball p ε ∧ IsOpen (ball p ε)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.parametrisat.doc:
/-- The parametrisations `φ ↦ r (cos φ, sin φ)` of a circle and `(θ, φ) ↦ r (sin θ cos φ, sin θ sin φ, cos θ)` of a
sphere are continuous, since their components are (`r = 1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.parametrisat.statement:
theorem parametrisations_continuous (r : ℝ) :
    Continuous (fun φ : ℝ => (r * Real.cos φ, r * Real.sin φ)) ∧
      Continuous (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => r • sph q.1 q.2)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.projections_su.doc: /-- The projections onto non-empty factors are surjective. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.projections_su.statement:
theorem projections_surjective (X Y : Type) [Nonempty X] [Nonempty Y] :
    Function.Surjective (Prod.fst : X × Y → X) ∧ Function.Surjective (Prod.snd : X × Y → Y)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.injective_iff.doc: /-- A map is injective exactly when every point of the codomain has at most one preimage. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.injective_iff.statement:
theorem injective_iff_preimage_subsingleton {X Y : Type} (f : X → Y) :
    Function.Injective f ↔ ∀ y, (f ⁻¹' {y}).Subsingleton

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.zmod_ops.doc: /-- The operations of `ℤₙ` on remainders: `(a + b) mod n` and `(a b) mod n` (the tables of `ℤ₃` and `ℤ₅`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.zmod_ops.statement:
theorem zmod_ops (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (a b : ZMod n) :
    (a + b).val = (a.val + b.val) % n ∧ (a * b).val = (a.val * b.val) % n

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.sqrt_prime_irratio.doc: /-- The square root of a prime is irrational (`√2 ∉ ℚ`): `ℚ ⊊ ℝ`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.sqrt_prime_irratio.statement: theorem sqrt_prime_irrational (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : Irrational (Real.sqrt p)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.card_t.doc: /-- The number of topologies on a finite type is the number of families satisfying the finite axioms. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.card_t.statement:
theorem card_topologies (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
    Nat.card (TopologicalSpace α) = (Finset.univ.filter fun F : Finset (Finset α) => IsFinTop F).card

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.multiples_of_f.doc: /-- The multiples of `4` fall into the classes `[0], [4], [8]` of `ℤ₁₂`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.multiples_of_f.statement: theorem multiples_of_four (k : ℤ) (hk : 4 ∣ k) : (k : ZMod 12) = 0 ∨ (k : ZMod 12) = 4 ∨ (k : ZMod 12) = 8

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.quotient_compac.doc: /-- A quotient of a compact space is compact: every coset space `S/R` of a compact group, `SO(3)/SO(2)` among them. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.quotient_compac.statement:
theorem quotient_compact (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [CompactSpace X] (s : Setoid X) :
    CompactSpace (Quotient s)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.orbit_quotien.doc:
/-- For `p₀` on the sphere, the quotient of `SO(3)` by "same image of `p₀`" is the sphere: `[g] ↦ g · p₀` is a
bijection onto it (for the north pole, the quotient by "same image of the pole"). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.orbit_quotien.statement:
theorem orbit_quotient_bijective (p₀ : Fin 3 → ℝ) (hp₀ : p₀ ∈ sphere) :
    ∃ F : Quotient (orbitSetoid p₀) → sphere, Function.Bijective F ∧
      ∀ g : SO3t, (F ⟦g⟧ : Fin 3 → ℝ) = (g : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) *ᵥ p₀

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.unique_remaind.doc:
/-- Every integer has exactly one remainder `0 ≤ r < n` modulo `n ≥ 1`: the classes `[0], …, [n - 1]` cover `ℤ` and are
distinct (`[0] = 3ℤ`, `[1] = 1 + 3ℤ`, `[2] = 2 + 3ℤ` for `n = 3`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.unique_remaind.statement: theorem unique_remainder (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (a : ℤ) : ∃! r : ℕ, r < n ∧ a ≡ r [ZMOD n]

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.extreme_values.doc: /-- A continuous real function on a non-empty compact set is bounded and attains its maximum and minimum. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.extreme_values.statement:
theorem extreme_values (E : Type) [TopologicalSpace E] (K : Set E) (hK : IsCompact K) (hne : K.Nonempty) (f : E → ℝ)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f K) :
    BddAbove (f '' K) ∧ BddBelow (f '' K) ∧ (∃ a ∈ K, IsMaxOn f K a) ∧ ∃ b ∈ K, IsMinOn f K b

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.bijective_iff.doc: /-- A map is a bijection exactly when every element of the codomain is the value of exactly one element. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.bijective_iff.statement: theorem bijective_iff_existsUnique {X Y : Type} (f : X → Y) : Function.Bijective f ↔ ∀ y, ∃! x, f x = y

KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.circle.doc:
/-- `ℝ/Tℤ` (`T > 0`) is homeomorphic to the circle by `[φ] ↦ (cos(2πφ/T), sin(2πφ/T))`: a continuous bijection from
the compact quotient onto the Hausdorff circle (for `T = 2π`, `[φ] ↦ (cos φ, sin φ)`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.circle.statement:
theorem circle_quotient_homeomorph (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    ∃ e : Quotient (angleSetoid T) ≃ₜ circle, ∀ φ, (e ⟦φ⟧ : ℝ × ℝ) = wrap (2 * Real.pi * φ / T)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.circle_mi.doc: /-- The circle minus any point is connected: it is the image of an open interval of angles. -/

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.topol.doc:
/-- The topologies on `{1, 2}`: Sage lists four (indiscrete, the two Sierpiński topologies, discrete), and they are
exactly the families satisfying the axioms. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.topol.statement:
theorem topologies_two : ∃ L : List (Finset (Finset (Fin 2))), L.Nodup ∧ L.length = 4 ∧
    ∀ F : Finset (Finset (Fin 2)), F ∈ L ↔ IsFinTop F

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.SO2_orbit_bi.doc:
/-- `g ↦ g · (1, 0)` from `SO(2)` onto the circle is a bijection: each point of the circle is the image of exactly one
plane rotation. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.SO2_orbit_bi.statement: theorem SO2_orbit_bijective (p : ℝ × ℝ) (hp : p ∈ circle) : ∃! g, g ∈ SO2 ∧ (g 0 0, g 1 0) = p

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.Rz_mul.doc:
/-- About a common axis the angles add: `R_z(α) R_z(β) = R_z(α + β)` (the right side expanded by the addition
formulas). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.Rz_mul.statement: theorem Rz_mul (α β : ℝ) : Rz α * Rz β = Rz (α + β)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.mem_SO3_iff.doc: /-- `SO(3)` is cut out of the `3 × 3` matrices by `Rᵀ R = 1` and `det R = 1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.mem_SO3_iff.statement: theorem mem_SO3_iff (R : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) : R ∈ SO3 ↔ Rᵀ * R = 1 ∧ R.det = 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.card_perm_fix.doc:
/-- The permutations of an `(n + 1)`-element set fixing one element are the `n!` permutations of the others: the
`3! = 6` permutations of `{1, 2, 3, 4}` fixing `4`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.card_perm_fix.statement:
theorem card_perm_fixing (n : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1)) :
    Fintype.card {σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (n + 1)) // σ a = a} = n.factorial

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.surjections_4_.doc:
/-- The surjective maps from four elements to three: Sage lists `36 = 81 - 3 · 2⁴ + 3`, without repetition, and the
list contains exactly the surjective maps. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.surjections_4_.statement:
theorem surjections_4_3 : ∃ L : List (Fin 4 → Fin 3), L.Nodup ∧ L.length = 36 ∧
    ∀ f : Fin 4 → Fin 3, f ∈ L ↔ Function.Surjective f

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.card_powerset.doc: /-- A set with `k` elements has `2ᵏ` subsets: `2³ = 8` for `{a, b, c}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.card_powerset.statement: theorem card_powerset {α : Type} (s : Finset α) : s.powerset.card = 2 ^ s.card

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.range_sq_add.doc: /-- `x ↦ x² + c` has image `[c, ∞)`: `x²` has image `[0, ∞)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.range_sq_add.statement: theorem range_sq_add (c : ℝ) : Set.range (fun x : ℝ => x ^ 2 + c) = Set.Ici c

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Exercises.compact_to_ha.doc:
/-- A continuous bijection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism: it sends closed sets to
closed sets, so its inverse is continuous. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Exercises.compact_to_ha.statement:
theorem compact_to_hausdorff (X Y : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [CompactSpace X] [T2Space Y]
    (f : X → Y) (hf : Continuous f) (hb : Function.Bijective f) :
    IsClosedMap f ∧ ∃ e : X ≃ₜ Y, ∀ x, e x = f x

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.chain.doc: /-- A chain of subsets containing `∅` and the whole set is a topology: `{∅, {1}, {1, 2}, {1, 2, 3}}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.chain.statement:
theorem chain_isFinTop {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (F : Finset (Finset α))
    (hchain : ∀ U ∈ F, ∀ V ∈ F, U ⊆ V ∨ V ⊆ U) (h0 : ∅ ∈ F) (h1 : Finset.univ ∈ F) : IsFinTop F

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.circle_minus_.doc:
/-- Removing two points `wrap a`, `wrap b` (`a < b < a + 2π`) disconnects the circle into the two open arcs between
them. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.circle_minus_.statement:
theorem circle_minus_two_points (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (hb : b < a + 2 * Real.pi) :
    ¬ IsPreconnected (circle \ {wrap a, wrap b})

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.caps_and_entri.doc:
/-- A cap `{p · n > t}` of the sphere is open in the sphere, and the rotations whose `(i, j)` entry lies in an open
range `(a, b)` form an open set of `SO(3)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.caps_and_entri.statement:
theorem caps_and_entries_open (n : Fin 3 → ℝ) (t a b : ℝ) (i j : Fin 3) :
    IsOpen ((Subtype.val : sphere → (Fin 3 → ℝ)) ⁻¹' {p | t < p ⬝ᵥ n}) ∧
      IsOpen ((Subtype.val : SO3 → Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) ⁻¹' {g | g i j ∈ Ioo a b})

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.closed_part_no.doc:
/-- For `-1 < t < 1` the part `{Y ≥ t}` of the circle is not open in the circle: every arc around the point
`(√(1 - t²), t)` contains points with `Y < t` (the closed upper half for `t = 0`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.closed_part_no.statement:
theorem closed_part_not_open (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1) :
    ¬ IsOpen ((Subtype.val : circle → ℝ × ℝ) ⁻¹' {p | t ≤ p.2})

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.points_closed.doc: /-- In a Hausdorff space every point is closed. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.points_closed.statement: theorem points_closed (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] (p : X) : IsClosed ({p} : Set X)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.orbit_fiber.doc:
/-- The rotations sending the pole where `g₀` does are the `g₀ h` with `h` fixing the pole: the preimage of every
point is a copy of the rotations about the `Z`-axis. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.orbit_fiber.statement:
theorem orbit_fiber (g₀ g : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) (hg₀ : g₀ ∈ SO3) :
    (g ∈ SO3 ∧ orbit g = orbit g₀) ↔ ∃ α, g = g₀ * Rz α

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.rotations_joi.doc:
/-- Every rotation is joined to the identity by a path of rotations about its axis, and no path in `O(3)` joins a
rotation to a reflection (the determinant would have to jump from `1` to `-1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.rotations_joi.statement:
theorem rotations_joined (R g : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) (hR : R ∈ SO3) (hg : g ∈ O3) (hdg : g.det = -1) :
    JoinedIn SO3 1 R ∧ ¬ JoinedIn O3 R g

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.closed_interval.doc:
/-- For `[0, c]` the family misses the endpoints `0` and `c`; open sets around them contain `(-ε, ε)` and
`(c - ε, c + ε)`, and together with one `U_N` (`c/(N + 2) < ε`) they cover `[0, c]`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.closed_interval.statement:
theorem closed_interval_cover (c ε : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (hε : 0 < ε) (N : ℕ) (hN : c / (N + 2) < ε) :
    (0 : ℝ) ∉ ⋃ n : ℕ, Ioo (c / (n + 2)) c ∧ c ∉ ⋃ n : ℕ, Ioo (c / (n + 2)) c ∧
      Icc 0 c ⊆ Ioo (-ε) ε ∪ Ioo (c - ε) (c + ε) ∪ Ioo (c / (N + 2)) c

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.multiples_disc.doc: /-- The multiples `Tℤ` (`T > 0`) are a discrete subspace of `ℝ`: `ℤ` for `T = 1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.multiples_disc.statement: theorem multiples_discrete (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) : DiscreteTopology (range (fun k : ℤ => (k : ℝ) * T))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.torus_point_r3.doc:
/-- The torus of revolution with radii `2` and `1`, `((2 + cos v) cos u, (2 + cos v) sin u, sin v)`, at
`(u, v) = (π/3, π/2)` is the point `(1, √3, 1)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.torus_point_r3.statement:
theorem torus_point_r3 :
    (2 + Real.cos (Real.pi / 2)) * Real.cos (Real.pi / 3) = 1 ∧
      (2 + Real.cos (Real.pi / 2)) * Real.sin (Real.pi / 3) = Real.sqrt 3 ∧ Real.sin (Real.pi / 2) = 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.doubled_point.doc:
/-- The line with the point `c` doubled is not Hausdorff: the two copies of `c` are distinct, but any neighbourhoods of
them meet (the line with two origins, `c = 0`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.doubled_point.statement:
theorem doubled_point_not_hausdorff (c : ℝ) :
    Quotient.mk (doubledSetoid c) (c, false) ≠ Quotient.mk (doubledSetoid c) (c, true) ∧
      ¬ T2Space (Quotient (doubledSetoid c))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.rot2_path.doc: /-- A path of plane rotations `t ↦ rot2 (tα)` from the identity to `rot2 α`, with determinant `1` throughout. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.rot2_path.statement: theorem rot2_path (α t : ℝ) : (rot2 (t * α)).det = 1 ∧ rot2 (0 * α) = 1 ∧ rot2 (1 * α) = rot2 α

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.range_mul_si.doc: /-- `x ↦ a sin x` (`a ≥ 0`) has image `[-a, a]`: `sin` has image `[-1, 1]`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.range_mul_si.statement: theorem range_mul_sin (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : Set.range (fun x => a * Real.sin x) = Set.Icc (-a) a

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.Rz_mul_Rz_neg.doc: /-- `R_z(α) R_z(-α) = 1`: the rotation by `-α` undoes the rotation by `α`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.Rz_mul_Rz_neg.statement: theorem Rz_mul_Rz_neg (α : ℝ) : Rz α * Rz (-α) = 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.coordinate_image_s.doc: /-- Each coordinate function on the sphere has image `[-1, 1]`: the height function `Z` (coordinate `2`) among them. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.coordinate_image_s.statement: theorem coordinate_image_sphere (i : Fin 3) : (fun p : Fin 3 → ℝ => p i) '' sphere = Set.Icc (-1) 1

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.comp_continu.doc: /-- The composition of continuous maps is continuous: `(g ∘ f)⁻¹(W) = f⁻¹(g⁻¹(W))`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.comp_continu.statement:
theorem comp_continuous (X Y Z : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [TopologicalSpace Z] (f : X → Y)
    (g : Y → Z) (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g) : Continuous (g ∘ f) ∧ ∀ W : Set Z, (g ∘ f) ⁻¹' W =
      f ⁻¹' (g ⁻¹' W)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.card_injectio.doc:
/-- There are `n (n - 1) ⋯ (n - m + 1)` injective maps from an `m`-element set to an `n`-element set: `4 · 3 · 2 =
24` from three elements to four. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.card_injectio.statement: theorem card_injections (m n : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Fin m ↪ Fin n) = n.descFactorial m

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.descFactorial_.doc: /-- No injective map exists from `m` elements to `n < m`: the falling factorial `n(n-1)⋯(n-m+1)` vanishes. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.descFactorial_.statement: theorem descFactorial_eq_zero (m n : ℕ) (h : n < m) : n.descFactorial m = 0

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.infinite_rn.statement: theorem infinite_rn (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : Infinite (Fin n → ℝ)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.multiples_clos.doc: /-- The multiples `Tℤ` (`T > 0`) form a closed, not open, subset of `ℝ`: `ℤ` for `T = 1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.multiples_clos.statement:
theorem multiples_closed_not_open (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    IsClosed (range (fun k : ℤ => (k : ℝ) * T)) ∧ ¬ IsOpen (range (fun k : ℤ => (k : ℝ) * T))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.rotations_con.doc:
/-- Any two rotations are joined by a path of rotations: `t ↦ R₁ R(t)` with `R(t)` the path from the identity to
`R₁⁻¹ R₂`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.rotations_con.statement:
theorem rotations_connect (R₁ R₂ : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) (h₁ : R₁ ∈ SO3) (h₂ : R₂ ∈ SO3) :
    JoinedIn SO3 R₁ R₂

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.cycle_inver.doc: /-- The inverse of `t` (Sage: `(1 3 2)`, as `0 ↦ 2 ↦ 1 ↦ 0`): `t ∘ t⁻¹ = t⁻¹ ∘ t = id`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.cycle_inver.statement: theorem cycle_inverse : ∃ u : Equiv.Perm (Fin 3), cycleT * u = 1 ∧ u * cycleT = 1 ∧ u 0 = 2 ∧ u 2 = 1 ∧ u 1 = 0

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.affine_unique.doc: /-- `ax + b = y` (`a ≠ 0`) has the unique solution `x = (y - b)/a`: `x = (y - 1)/2` for `2x + 1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.affine_unique.statement: theorem affine_unique_solution (a b y : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) : ∃! x, a * x + b = y ∧ x = (y - b) / a

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.Icc_not_h.doc: /-- A closed interval is not homeomorphic to an open one (the first is compact, the second is not). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.Icc_not_h.statement: theorem Icc_not_homeomorph_Ioo (a b c d : ℝ) (hab : a ≤ b) (hcd : c < d) : IsEmpty (Icc a b ≃ₜ Ioo c d)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.surjective_i.doc: /-- A map from a finite set to itself is surjective exactly when it is injective (a bijection). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.surjective_i.statement:
theorem surjective_iff_injective_self (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → Fin n) :
    Function.Surjective f ↔ Function.Injective f

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Maps.finite_map_image_p.statement:
theorem finite_map_image_preimage {β : Type} (x y : β) (hxy : x ≠ y) :
    Set.range ![x, x, y] = {x, y} ∧ ![x, x, y] ⁻¹' {x} = {0, 1}

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.continuous_i.doc: /-- Between metric spaces (subsets of `ℝⁿ`), continuity is the ε-δ condition. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.continuous_i.statement:
theorem continuous_iff_eps_delta (X Y : Type) [MetricSpace X] [MetricSpace Y] (f : X → Y) :
    Continuous f ↔ ∀ p, ∀ ε > 0, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ x, dist x p < δ → dist (f x) (f p) < ε

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.odd_pow_surj.doc: /-- Odd powers are surjective onto `ℝ` (every real number has a cube root, `k = 1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.odd_pow_surj.statement: theorem odd_pow_surjective (k : ℕ) : Function.Surjective (fun x : ℝ => x ^ (2 * k + 1))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.double_not_inje.doc: /-- Doubling on `ℤ₆` is not injective: two distinct elements with the same double (Sage finds `0` and `3`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.double_not_inje.statement: theorem double_not_injective : ∃ a b : ZMod 6, a ≠ b ∧ 2 * a = 2 * b

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.range_mul_ex.doc: /-- `x ↦ a eˣ` (`a > 0`) has image the positive numbers: `exp` is not surjective onto `ℝ`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.range_mul_ex.statement: theorem range_mul_exp (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) : Set.range (fun x => a * Real.exp x) = Set.Ioi 0

KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.torus_.doc:
/-- Identifying the opposite edges of `[0, L]²` (`L > 0`) gives a space homeomorphic to the torus `S¹ × S¹` by
`(u, v) ↦ ((cos(2πu/L), sin(2πu/L)), (cos(2πv/L), sin(2πv/L)))` (for `L = 2π`, `(u, v) ↦ ((cos u, sin u), (cos v,
sin v))`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.QuotientTopology.torus_.statement:
theorem torus_quotient_homeomorph (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) :
    ∃ e : Quotient (squareSetoid L) ≃ₜ (circle ×ˢ circle : Set ((ℝ × ℝ) × (ℝ × ℝ))),
      ∀ p : square L, (e ⟦p⟧ : (ℝ × ℝ) × (ℝ × ℝ)) =
        (wrap (2 * Real.pi * p.1.1 / L), wrap (2 * Real.pi * p.1.2 / L))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.reciprocals_ze.doc:
/-- With `0` added, the subspace is not discrete: every open set of `ℝ` containing `0` contains infinitely many
`c/n`, so `{0}` is not open in it. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.reciprocals_ze.statement:
theorem reciprocals_zero_not_discrete (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    ¬ DiscreteTopology ↥(insert (0 : ℝ) (range (fun n : ℕ => c / (n + 1))) : Set ℝ)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.tan_homeo.doc:
/-- `x ↦ a tan x` (`a > 0`) is a homeomorphism from `(-π/2, π/2)` onto `ℝ`: an open interval and the whole line are
homeomorphic (`tan` for `a = 1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.tan_homeo.statement:
theorem tan_homeomorph (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∃ e : Ioo (-(Real.pi / 2)) (Real.pi / 2) ≃ₜ ℝ, ∀ x, e x = a * Real.tan x

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.figureEig.doc: /-- The figure eight minus its crossing point is not connected: it splits into the parts `X > 0` and `X < 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.figureEig.statement:
theorem figureEight_minus_origin_not_connected (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) :
    ¬ IsPreconnected (figureEight r \ {(0, 0)})

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.hyperboloid_not.doc:
/-- The hyperboloid `-t² + x² + y² + z² = ℓ²` (de Sitter space) is not compact: it is unbounded, containing
`(t, √(ℓ² + t²), 0, 0)` for every `t`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.hyperboloid_not.statement:
theorem hyperboloid_not_compact (ℓ : ℝ) :
    ¬ IsCompact {p : Fin 4 → ℝ | -p 0 ^ 2 + p 1 ^ 2 + p 2 ^ 2 + p 3 ^ 2 = ℓ ^ 2}

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.isFin.doc: /-- On a finite set, the decidable axioms `IsFinTop` are the axioms of a topology. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.isFin.statement:
theorem isFinTop_iff {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (F : Finset (Finset α)) :
    IsFinTop F ↔ IsTopologyOn α ((fun V : Finset α => (V : Set α)) '' (F : Set (Finset α)))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.disc_inclusions.doc:
/-- For the discs and circle of radius `√r`: the open disc lies in the closed one, the circle lies in the closed disc
and misses the open one (`r = 1` for `S¹ ⊆ D`, `S¹ ∩ {X² + Y² < 1} = ∅`). -/

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.cofinite_not_.doc:
/-- The converse fails: on an infinite set the cofinite topology has closed points but is not Hausdorff (two non-empty
open sets always meet). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.cofinite_not_.statement:
theorem cofinite_not_hausdorff (X : Type) [Infinite X] :
    T1Space (CofiniteTopology X) ∧ ¬ T2Space (CofiniteTopology X)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.surjective_o.doc: /-- Every map is surjective onto its image. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.surjective_o.statement: theorem surjective_onto_range {X Y : Type} (f : X → Y) : Function.Surjective (Set.rangeFactorization f)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.cover_no_finite.doc:
/-- The sets `U_n = (c/n, c)`, `n ≥ 2` (`c > 0`), cover `(0, c)`, but no finite subfamily does: the members with
`n < N + 2` all miss `c/(N + 2)` (the cover of `(0, 1)` by `(1/n, 1)` for `c = 1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.cover_no_finite.statement:
theorem cover_no_finite_subcover (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    (⋃ n : ℕ, Ioo (c / (n + 2)) c) = Ioo 0 c ∧
      ∀ N : ℕ, c / (N + 2) ∈ Ioo 0 c ∧ c / (N + 2) ∉ ⋃ n ∈ Finset.range N, Ioo (c / (n + 2)) c

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.pathConnected.statement:
theorem pathConnected_connected (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (S : Set X) (h : IsPathConnected S) :
    IsConnected S

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.id_not_period.doc: /-- `φ ↦ φ` does not descend: it is not periodic for any period `T ≠ 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.id_not_period.statement: theorem id_not_periodic (T : ℝ) (hT : T ≠ 0) : ¬ Function.Periodic (fun φ : ℝ => φ) T

KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.intervals_open.doc: /-- For `a < b`: `(a, b)` is open, `[a, b]` is closed and not open, `[a, b)` is neither (`a = 0`, `b = 2π`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.intervals_open.statement:
theorem intervals_open_closed (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) :
    IsOpen (Ioo a b) ∧ (IsClosed (Icc a b) ∧ ¬ IsOpen (Icc a b)) ∧ (¬ IsOpen (Ico a b) ∧ ¬ IsClosed (Ico a b))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.swap_cycle_.doc: /-- `t ∘ s ≠ s ∘ t`: a point where the two compositions differ (Sage finds it). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.swap_cycle_.statement: theorem swap_cycle_noncommute : ∃ x : Fin 3, cycleT (swapS x) ≠ swapS (cycleT x)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.quotient_desc.doc: /-- The quotient map `x ↦ [x]` is surjective, and a map constant on classes descends: `f = f̄ ∘ π`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.quotient_desc.statement:
theorem quotient_descends {X Y : Type} (s : Setoid X) (f : X → Y) (hf : ∀ a b, s a b → f a = f b) :
    Function.Surjective (Quotient.mk s) ∧ (fun x => Quotient.lift f hf (Quotient.mk s x)) = f

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.O3_components.doc:
/-- `O(3)` has two connected components, the rotations (`det = 1`) and the reflections (`det = -1`): the component of
`g` is the set of orthogonal matrices with the determinant of `g`, since the determinant is continuous with values
`±1`, and each of the two sets is a translate of the connected `SO(3)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.O3_components.statement:
theorem O3_components (g : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) (hg : g ∈ O3) :
    connectedComponentIn O3 g = {h ∈ O3 | h.det = g.det}

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.cos_two_mul_p.doc: /-- `cos 2φ` is `2π`-periodic and descends to the circle. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.cos_two_mul_p.statement: theorem cos_two_mul_periodic (φ : ℝ) : Real.cos (2 * (φ + 2 * Real.pi)) = Real.cos (2 * φ)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.card_perm.doc: /-- There are `n!` permutations of an `n`-element set: `3! = 6`, `4! = 24`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.card_perm.statement: theorem card_perm (n : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) = n.factorial

KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.finer_.doc:
/-- A finer topology on the domain keeps every continuous map continuous; a finer topology on the codomain can only
lose continuous maps (a map continuous into the finer one is continuous into the coarser one). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.finer_.statement:
theorem finer_coarser (X Y : Type) (t₁ t₂ : TopologicalSpace X) (s₁ s₂ : TopologicalSpace Y) (f : X → Y)
    (ht : t₂ ≤ t₁) (hs : s₂ ≤ s₁) :
    (Continuous[t₁, s₁] f → Continuous[t₂, s₁] f) ∧ (Continuous[t₁, s₂] f → Continuous[t₁, s₁] f)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.intervals_compa.doc: /-- For `a < b`: `[a, b]` is compact, `(a, b)` is not, and `ℝ` is not (`[0, 1]` and `(0, 1)`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.intervals_compa.statement:
theorem intervals_compact (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) :
    IsCompact (Icc a b) ∧ ¬ IsCompact (Ioo a b) ∧ ¬ IsCompact (univ : Set ℝ)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.corners_one_c.doc: /-- The four corners of `[0, 1]²` are all identified: any two corners are related, one class. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.corners_one_c.statement:
theorem corners_one_class (c c' : ℝ × ℝ) (hc : (c.1 = 0 ∨ c.1 = 1) ∧ (c.2 = 0 ∨ c.2 = 1))
    (hc' : (c'.1 = 0 ∨ c'.1 = 1) ∧ (c'.2 = 0 ∨ c'.2 = 1)) : Relation.EqvGen (glue 1) c c'

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.inverse_com.doc: /-- A bijection and its inverse compose to the identities: `f⁻¹ ∘ f = id_X`, `f ∘ f⁻¹ = id_Y`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.inverse_com.statement: theorem inverse_comp {X Y : Type} (e : X ≃ Y) : e.symm ∘ e = id ∧ e ∘ e.symm = id

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.union.doc:
/-- On three points the union of two topologies need not be one: Sage finds `{∅, {1}, X}` and `{∅, {2}, X}`, whose union
lacks `{1, 2}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.union.statement: theorem union_not_topology : ∃ F G : Finset (Finset (Fin 3)), IsFinTop F ∧ IsFinTop G ∧ ¬ IsFinTop (F ∪ G)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.deriv_x_d.doc: /-- The derivative `(1 + x²)/(1 - x²)²` is positive on `(-1, 1)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.deriv_x_d.statement: theorem deriv_x_div_pos (x : ℝ) (hx : x ∈ Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1) : 0 < (1 + x ^ 2) / (1 - x ^ 2) ^ 2

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.discr.doc: /-- On any set, all subsets (discrete) and `{∅, X}` (indiscrete) are topologies. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.discr.statement: theorem discrete_indiscrete (X : Type) : IsTopologyOn X univ ∧ IsTopologyOn X {∅, univ}

KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.sierpi.doc:
/-- In the Sierpiński space: it is a topology; every neighbourhood of `y` contains `x` exactly when `x = 1` or
`x = y` (the neighbourhoods of `1` are `{1}` and `{1, 2}`, the only one of `2` is `{1, 2}`; so the constant sequence
`1, 1, …` converges to both points); a point `x` is closed exactly when `x = 2`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.sierpi.statement:
theorem sierpinski_facts (x y : Fin 2) :
    IsFinTop sierpinski ∧ ((∀ U ∈ sierpinski, y ∈ U → x ∈ U) ↔ (x = 0 ∨ x = y)) ∧
      (({x}ᶜ : Finset (Fin 2)) ∈ sierpinski ↔ x = 1)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.t0_top.doc: /-- The `T₀` topologies on three points: Sage lists `19`, and they are exactly the topologies that separate points. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.FiniteTopologies.t0_top.statement:
theorem t0_topologies_three : ∃ L : List (Finset (Finset (Fin 3))), L.Nodup ∧ L.length = 19 ∧
    ∀ F : Finset (Finset (Fin 3)), F ∈ L ↔ IsFinTop F ∧ IsT0Fin F

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.moebius_f_finv.statement: theorem moebius_f_finv (y w : ℝ) (hw : (1 - y) * w = 1) : (1 + y) * w - 1 = y * ((1 + y) * w + 1)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.half_open_rela.doc:
/-- For `0 < c ≤ 1`: `[0, c) = (-c, c) ∩ [0, 1)` is open in the subspace `[0, 1)` but not open in `ℝ`
(`c = ½`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.half_open_rela.statement:
theorem half_open_relative (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (hc1 : c ≤ 1) :
    Ico 0 c = Ioo (-c) c ∩ Ico 0 1 ∧ IsOpen ((Subtype.val : Ico (0 : ℝ) 1 → ℝ) ⁻¹' Ico 0 c) ∧
      ¬ IsOpen (Ico (0 : ℝ) c)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.rat_quotient_.doc:
/-- The quotient of `ℝ` by `x ∼ y` iff `x - y ∈ cℚ` (`c > 0`) is not Hausdorff: every open set is empty or everything,
since every open interval meets every class (`c = 1`: the quotient `ℝ/ℚ`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.rat_quotient_.statement:
theorem rat_quotient_not_hausdorff (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    (∀ V : Set (Quotient (ratSetoid c)), IsOpen V → V = ∅ ∨ V = univ) ∧ ¬ T2Space (Quotient (ratSetoid c))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.x_div_hom.doc:
/-- `x ↦ a x/(1 - x²)` (`a > 0`) is a homeomorphism from `(-1, 1)` onto `ℝ`, with inverse
`y ↦ 2y/(a + √(a² + 4y²))` (`a = 1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.x_div_hom.statement:
theorem x_div_homeomorph (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∃ e : Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1 ≃ₜ ℝ, ∀ x, e x = a * x / (1 - (x : ℝ) ^ 2)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.card_bijection.doc: /-- Bijections between an `m`-element and an `n`-element set: `n!` when `m = n` and none otherwise. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Counting.card_bijection.statement: theorem card_bijections (m n : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Fin m ≃ Fin n) = if m = n then n.factorial else 0

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.zmod_cyclic.doc: /-- `ℤₙ` is cyclic, generated by `1`: every element is a multiple of `1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Products.zmod_cyclic.statement: theorem zmod_cyclic (n : ℕ) (a : ZMod n) : ∃ k : ℤ, a = k • (1 : ZMod n)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.class_angle.doc:
/-- Every interval `[a, a + T)` of length `T > 0` contains exactly one member of the class `{φ + kT}`: the class of an
angle has one angle in every interval of length `2π`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Equivalence.class_angle.statement:
theorem class_angle_unique (T a φ : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    ∃! ψ, ψ ∈ Set.Ico a (a + T) ∧ ∃ k : ℤ, ψ = φ + k * T

KaluzaKlein.Sets.OpenSets.punctured_open.statement: theorem punctured_open (n : ℕ) (p : Fin n → ℝ) : IsOpen ({p}ᶜ : Set (Fin n → ℝ))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.moebius_finv_f.statement: theorem moebius_finv_f (x t : ℝ) (ht : (x + 1) * t = 1) : 1 + (x - 1) * t = x * (1 - (x - 1) * t)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.parti.doc: /-- `∅` together with all the sets containing a point `a` is a topology: `{∅, {1}, {1, 2}, {1, 3}, X}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.parti.statement:
theorem particular_point_isFinTop {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (a : α) :
    IsFinTop (insert ∅ (Finset.univ.filter (fun U : Finset α => a ∈ U)))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.mul_sin_not_.doc: /-- `x ↦ a sin x` (`a ≥ 0`) is not surjective onto `ℝ` (it misses `a + 1`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.mul_sin_not_.statement: theorem mul_sin_not_surjective (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : ¬ Function.Surjective (fun x => a * Real.sin x)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.rotations_n.doc: /-- The `(1, 3)` entries are `sin α sin β` and `0`, so the products differ whenever `sin α sin β ≠ 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Composition.rotations_n.statement: theorem rotations_noncommute (α β : ℝ) (h : Real.sin α * Real.sin β ≠ 0) : Rz α * Rx β ≠ Rx β * Rz α

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.card_zmod.doc: /-- `ℤ/nℤ` has `n` elements (`n ≥ 1`): three for `n = 3`, five for `n = 5`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Quotients.card_zmod.statement: theorem card_zmod (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : Fintype.card (ZMod n) = n

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.wrap_bijOn.doc:
/-- `φ ↦ (cos φ, sin φ)` restricted to `(a, a + 2π)` is a bijection onto the circle minus the point of angle `a`: on
`(0, 2π)` onto the circle minus `(1, 0)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.wrap_bijOn.statement: theorem wrap_bijOn (a : ℝ) : Set.BijOn wrap (Set.Ioo a (a + 2 * Real.pi)) (circle \ {wrap a})

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.card_rotations.doc:
/-- The rotations of the plane by the multiples of `360°/n`, the `n`-th roots of unity, are `n` in number: six for
the hexagon. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.card_rotations.statement: theorem card_rotations (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : Nat.card (rootsOfUnity n ℂ) = n

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.deriv_x_d.doc: /-- `x ↦ x/(1 - x²)` has derivative `(1 + x²)/(1 - x²)²` where `x² ≠ 1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.deriv_x_d.statement:
theorem deriv_x_div (x : ℝ) (hx : 1 - x ^ 2 ≠ 0) :
    deriv (fun x : ℝ => x / (1 - x ^ 2)) x = (1 + x ^ 2) / (1 - x ^ 2) ^ 2

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.not_t.doc: /-- `{∅, {1, 2}, {2, 3}, X}` is not a topology: two members whose intersection is missing (Sage finds `{2}`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.not_t.statement:
theorem not_topology_inter : ∃ U ∈ ({∅, {0, 1}, {1, 2}, Finset.univ} : Finset (Finset (Fin 3))),
    ∃ V ∈ ({∅, {0, 1}, {1, 2}, Finset.univ} : Finset (Finset (Fin 3))),
      U ∩ V ∉ ({∅, {0, 1}, {1, 2}, Finset.univ} : Finset (Finset (Fin 3)))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.sph_pole.doc: /-- Every `(0, φ)` is sent to the north pole: on `[0, π] × [0, 2π)` the pole has infinitely many preimages. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Injective.sph_pole.statement: theorem sph_pole (φ : ℝ) : sph 0 φ = northPole

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.affine_biject.doc: /-- `x ↦ ax + b` (`a ≠ 0`) is a bijection of `ℝ`: `2x + 1` among them. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.affine_biject.statement: theorem affine_bijective (a b : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) : Function.Bijective (fun x : ℝ => a * x + b)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Bijective.int_affine.doc: /-- On `ℤ`, `k ↦ 2k + b` (`b` odd) is injective, not surjective, and its image is the odd integers: `2k + 1`. -/

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.cbrt_inverse.statement: theorem cbrt_inverse (x y : ℝ) : cbrt (x ^ 3) = x ∧ cbrt y ^ 3 = y

KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.not_t.doc: /-- `{∅, {1}, {2}, {1, 2, 3}}` is not a topology: two members whose union is missing (Sage finds `{1} ∪ {2}`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.TopologicalSpaces.not_t.statement:
theorem not_topology_union : ∃ U ∈ ({∅, {0}, {1}, Finset.univ} : Finset (Finset (Fin 3))),
    ∃ V ∈ ({∅, {0}, {1}, Finset.univ} : Finset (Finset (Fin 3))),
      U ∪ V ∉ ({∅, {0}, {1}, Finset.univ} : Finset (Finset (Fin 3)))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.discrete_indi.doc: /-- The discrete topology is Hausdorff; the indiscrete topology on a set with two distinct points is not. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Hausdorff.discrete_indi.statement:
theorem discrete_indiscrete_hausdorff (X : Type) (x y : X) (hxy : x ≠ y) :
    @T2Space X ⊥ ∧ ¬ @T2Space X ⊤

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.figureEig.doc:
/-- A figure eight is not homeomorphic to the circle: removing the crossing point leaves two pieces, while removing a
point from the circle leaves one. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Homeomorphism.figureEig.statement: theorem figureEight_not_homeomorph_circle (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) : IsEmpty (figureEight r ≃ₜ circle)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.arc_open.doc:
/-- An open arc of the circle, the angles within `δ ≤ π` of `c`, is the trace on the circle of the open half-plane
`{p · (cos c, sin c) > cos δ}`, hence open in the circle. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Subspace.arc_open.statement:
theorem arc_open (c δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδπ : δ ≤ Real.pi) :
    wrap '' Ioo (c - δ) (c + δ) = circle ∩ {p | Real.cos δ < p.1 * Real.cos c + p.2 * Real.sin c} ∧
      IsOpen ((Subtype.val : circle → ℝ × ℝ) ⁻¹' (wrap '' Ioo (c - δ) (c + δ)))

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.plane_disc_not_.doc: /-- `ℝⁿ` (`n ≥ 1`) is not compact, nor is the open disc of radius `√r` (`r > 0`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Compact.plane_disc_not_.statement:
theorem plane_disc_not_compact (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) :
    ¬ IsCompact (univ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) ∧ ¬ IsCompact {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.1 ^ 2 + p.2 ^ 2 < r}

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.stabilizer_e.doc: /-- The rotations fixing the north pole are exactly the rotations `Rz α` about the `Z`-axis, a copy of `SO(2)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Surjective.stabilizer_e.statement: theorem stabilizer_eq (h : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) : (h ∈ SO3 ∧ orbit h = northPole) ↔ ∃ α, h = Rz α

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.moebius_bijOn.doc:
/-- `x ↦ (x - a)/(x + a)` (`a ≠ 0`) is a bijection of `ℝ ∖ {-a}` onto `ℝ ∖ {1}` with inverse
`y ↦ a (1 + y)/(1 - y)`: for `a = 1`, `f(x) = (x - 1)/(x + 1)` and `f⁻¹(y) = (1 + y)/(1 - y)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Inverse.moebius_bijOn.statement:
theorem moebius_bijOn (a : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    Set.BijOn (fun x => (x - a) / (x + a)) {x | x ≠ -a} {y | y ≠ 1} ∧
      (∀ y, y ≠ 1 → (a * (1 + y) / (1 - y) - a) / (a * (1 + y) / (1 - y) + a) = y) ∧
      (∀ x, x ≠ -a → a * (1 + (x - a) / (x + a)) / (1 - (x - a) / (x + a)) = x)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.step_not_con.doc:
/-- The step function at `a` is not continuous: the preimage of the open interval `(½, 2)` is `[a, ∞)`, which is not
open (`a = 0`). -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Continuous.step_not_con.statement:
theorem step_not_continuous (a : ℝ) :
    step a ⁻¹' Ioo (1 / 2) 2 = Ici a ∧ ¬ IsOpen (Ici a) ∧ ¬ Continuous (step a)

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.neg_not_nat.doc: /-- A negative integer is not a natural number (`-1 ∉ ℕ`): `ℕ ⊊ ℤ`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Sets.Sets.neg_not_nat.statement: theorem neg_not_nat (z : ℤ) (hz : z < 0) : ¬ ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℤ) = z

KaluzaKlein.Sets.Connected.connected_of_.doc:
