    Set.Icc (-a) a ∩ Set.Icc (x - a) (x + a) = Set.Icc (x - a) a ∧ ∫ y in (x - a)..a, (1 : ℝ) = 2 * a - x

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeriodicFunc.doc: /-- No `T ∈ (0, 2π)` is a period of `sin`: `2π` is the smallest period. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeriodicFunc.statement:
theorem sin_no_smaller_period (T : ℝ) (h0 : 0 < T) (h1 : T < 2 * π) :
    Real.sin (π / 2 + T) ≠ Real.sin (π / 2)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Uncertainty..doc: /-- The second moment `∫ x² e^{-x²/σ²} = σ³√π/2`, from the Gamma integral. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Uncertainty..statement: theorem gaussian_second_moment (σ : ℝ) (hσ : 0 < σ) : ∫ x : ℝ, x ^ 2 * Real.exp (-x ^ 2 / σ ^ 2) = σ ^ 3 * Real.sqrt π / 2

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphericalHar.statement: theorem theta_int_11_1 : ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..π, (Real.sin t ^ 3) = 4/3

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TheTransform.doc: /-- The derivative rule `(f')^ = i k f̂` (through mathlib's `fourier_deriv`). -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TheTransform.statement:
theorem ft_deriv (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : Integrable f) (hd : Differentiable ℝ f) (hf' : Integrable (deriv f))
    (k : ℝ) : ft (deriv f) k = Complex.I * k * ft f k

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeriodicFunc.doc: /-- Right of `π` the sawtooth is `x - 2π`, so `f(π⁺) = -π`: the jump is `-2π`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeriodicFunc.statement: theorem sawtooth_right (t : ℝ) (h0 : 0 < t) (h1 : t ≤ 2 * π) : sawtooth (π + t) = t - π

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Parseval.bes.statement:
theorem bessel {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (s : Finset ι) (e : ι → E) (he : Orthonormal ℝ e) (f : E) :
    ∑ i ∈ s, (inner ℝ (e i) f) ^ 2 ≤ ‖f‖ ^ 2

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.CosetModes.h.doc: /-- A half-integer spin mode is odd under `ψ ↦ ψ + 2π`: `e^{-in(ψ+2π)/2} = (-1)^n e^{-inψ/2}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.CosetModes.h.statement:
theorem half_spin_odd (n : ℤ) (ψ : ℝ) :
    Complex.exp (-(n * (ψ + 2 * π) / 2) * Complex.I) = (-1) ^ n * Complex.exp (-(n * ψ / 2) * Complex.I)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PartialSums..statement: theorem dirichlet_integral (N : ℕ) : ∫ t in (-π)..π, dirichlet N t = 2 * π

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.HarmonicComp.doc:
/-- The Laplacian on homogeneous quadratics, from the monomials `x², y², z², xy, xz, yz` to the constants, is
`(2, 2, 2, 0, 0, 0)`, of rank `1`: the harmonic quadratics form a space of dimension `6 - 1 = 5`. -/

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PrincipalVal.doc: /-- The half-residue: `iπ e^{ia} = iπ cos a - π sin a`, whose real part is `-π sin a` (`a = 1` here). -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PrincipalVal.statement: theorem half_residue (a : ℝ) : (Complex.I * π * Complex.exp ((a : ℂ) * Complex.I)).re = -π * Real.sin a

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.MatrixCoeffi.doc: /-- Weyl orthonormality: `∫ χ₀ χ₀ dμ_W = 1` (`θ = 2t`, `dμ_W = (2/π) sin² t dt`). -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.MatrixCoeffi.statement: theorem weyl_0_0 : ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..π, 1 * 1 * (2 / π * Real.sin t ^ 2) = 1

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.doc: /-- `∫ g_ε eˣ = e^{ε²/4}`, by completing the square. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.statement:
theorem gauss_exp (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∫ x : ℝ, Real.exp (-x ^ 2 / ε ^ 2) / (ε * Real.sqrt π) * Real.exp x = Real.exp (ε ^ 2 / 4)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Parseval.bes.doc:
/-- The mean-square error of a finite combination of orthonormal modes:
`‖f - Σ tᵢ eᵢ‖² = ‖f‖² - Σ cᵢ² + Σ (cᵢ - tᵢ)²` with `cᵢ = ⟪eᵢ, f⟫`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Parseval.bes.statement:
theorem best_approx {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (s : Finset ι) (e : ι → E) (he : Orthonormal ℝ e) (f : E) (t : ι → ℝ) :
    ‖f - ∑ i ∈ s, t i • e i‖ ^ 2 =
      ‖f‖ ^ 2 - ∑ i ∈ s, (inner ℝ (e i) f) ^ 2 + ∑ i ∈ s, (inner ℝ (e i) f - t i) ^ 2

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SeriesComput.doc: /-- The cosine coefficients of the triangle wave `π/2 - |x|`: `2 (1 - cos n π) / (π n²)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SeriesComput.statement:
theorem triangle_an (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    2 / π * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π, (π / 2 - x) * Real.cos (n * x) = 2 * (1 - Real.cos (n * π)) / (π * n ^ 2)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphericalHar.statement: theorem cos_cos_two_phi : ∫ p in (0 : ℝ)..(2 * π), Real.cos p * Real.cos (2 * p) = 0

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.doc: /-- Left of `0`, `u = -eˣ/2` has slope `-1/2` at `0`: the jump of `u'` is `1`, the delta. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.statement: theorem green_slope_left : deriv (fun x : ℝ => -1 / 2 * Real.exp x) 0 = -1 / 2

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.doc: /-- The limits `e^{-ε²/4} → 1` and `1 + ε²/2 → 1` as `ε → 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.statement:
theorem gauss_limits (c : ℝ) : Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => c * Real.exp (-ε ^ 2 / 4)) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 c) ∧
    Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => c * (1 + ε ^ 2 / 2)) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 c)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeterWeyl.s3.doc: /-- The Casimir and the round `S³`: `-4j(j+1) = -n(n+2)` for `n = 2j`, with multiplicity `(2j+1)² = (n+1)²`. -/

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.HarmonicComp.doc: /-- `r³ Y₃₃ ∝ (x + iy)³`: `(sin θ cos φ + i sin θ sin φ)³ = sin³ θ e^{3iφ}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.HarmonicComp.statement:
theorem l3_top (θ φ : ℝ) :
    ((Real.sin θ * Real.cos φ : ℝ) + (Real.sin θ * Real.sin φ : ℝ) * Complex.I) ^ 3 =
      (Real.sin θ : ℂ) ^ 3 * Complex.exp (3 * φ * Complex.I)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SeriesComput.doc: /-- The sines are the Dirichlet modes of `-d²/dx²` on `[0, π]`: `-(sin n x)'' = n² sin n x`, vanishing at `0` and `π`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SeriesComput.statement:
theorem sine_dirichlet_mode (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    deriv (deriv fun y => Real.sin (n * y)) x = -(n : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.sin (n * x) ∧
      Real.sin (n * 0) = 0 ∧ Real.sin (n * π) = 0

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphereLaplac.doc: /-- The radial part: `(∂_r² + (2/r) ∂_r) r^l = l(l+1) r^{l-2}`, so `Δ Y = -l(l+1) Y` for `P = r^l Y` harmonic. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphereLaplac.statement:
theorem radial_power (l : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (hr : r ≠ 0) (hl : 2 ≤ l) :
    deriv (deriv fun r : ℝ => r ^ l) r + 2 / r * deriv (fun r : ℝ => r ^ l) r = l * (l + 1) * r ^ (l - 2)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Plancherel.e.statement: theorem exp_two_sided_l2 (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) : ∫ x : ℝ, Real.exp (-(2 * a) * |x|) = 1 / a

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PartialSums..statement:
theorem fejer_integral (N : ℕ) :
    ∫ t in (-π)..π, (1 / (N + 1 : ℝ)) * ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), dirichlet n t = 2 * π

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Convergence..doc: /-- The terms `cos n x` of the differentiated sawtooth series do not tend to `0`, at any `x`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Convergence..statement: theorem cos_mul_not_tendsto_zero (x : ℝ) : ¬ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.cos (n * x)) atTop (𝓝 0)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.doc:
/-- The Leibniz rule `(ψT)' = ψ'T + ψT'` for a linear functional `T`, with `T'(φ) = -T(φ')` and
`(ψT)(φ) = T(ψφ)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.statement:
theorem leibniz_rule (T : (ℝ → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (ψ φ : ℝ → ℝ) (hψ : Differentiable ℝ ψ) (hφ : Differentiable ℝ φ) :
    -T (ψ * deriv φ) = T (deriv ψ * φ) + -T (deriv (ψ * φ))

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeterWeyl.pw.doc: /-- Peter-Weyl for `U(1)` (mathlib): the characters `e^{inφ}` form a Hilbert basis of `L²` of the circle. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeterWeyl.pw.statement: theorem pw_circle (T : ℝ) [hT : Fact (0 < T)] : ⇑(@fourierBasis T hT) = fourierLp 2

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TestFunction.doc:
/-- The bump is not analytic at the edge of its support: `t ↦ e^{-1/(ct)}` is not analytic at `0` for any `c > 0`
(mathlib: `e^{-1/t}` is not analytic at `0`). -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TestFunction.statement: theorem not_analytic_edge (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) : ¬ AnalyticAt ℝ (fun t => expNegInvGlue (c * t)) 0

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TheTransform.doc: /-- The translation rule `(f(x - a))^ = e^{-ika} f̂`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TheTransform.statement:
theorem ft_translate (f : ℝ → ℂ) (a k : ℝ) :
    ft (fun x => f (x - a)) k = Complex.exp (-(k * a) * Complex.I) * ft f k

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PartialSums..doc: /-- The Fejér kernel `Σ_{n ≤ N} D_n` is non-negative. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PartialSums..statement: theorem fejer_nonneg (N : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : 0 ≤ ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), dirichlet n t

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Convergence..doc:
/-- (i) Dirichlet's theorem for the square wave, as stated (tested, not proved: Dirichlet's pointwise theorem for
piecewise `C¹` functions is not in mathlib): at every `x ∈ (0, π)` the partial sums tend to `sgn x = 1`. -/

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Inversion.in.doc:
/-- Fourier inversion (mathlib, in the normalisation `𝓕 f(w) = ∫ e^{-2πixw} f`): `𝓕⁻ (𝓕 f) = f` for continuous
integrable `f` with integrable transform. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Inversion.in.statement:
theorem inversion (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hc : Continuous f) (hf : Integrable f) (hf' : Integrable (𝓕 f)) :
    𝓕⁻ (𝓕 f) = f

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Inversion.ga.doc:
/-- The Gaussian approximate identity (mathlib): `∫ (πc)^{1/2} e^{-π²c|w - v|²} f(w) dw → f(v)` as `c → ∞` at a
point of continuity of an integrable `f`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Inversion.ga.statement:
theorem gaussian_approx_identity (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : Integrable f) (v : ℝ) (hv : ContinuousAt f v) :
    Tendsto (fun c : ℝ => ∫ w : ℝ, ((π * c : ℂ) ^ (Module.finrank ℝ ℝ / 2 : ℂ) *
      Complex.exp (-π ^ 2 * c * ‖v - w‖ ^ 2)) • f w) atTop (𝓝 (f v))

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeriodicFunc.statement: theorem squareWave_of_neg (x : ℝ) (h0 : -π < x) (h1 : x < 0) : squareWave x = -1

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Parseval.x_f.statement: theorem x_four_integral : ∫ x in (-π)..π, x ^ 4 = 2 * π ^ 5 / 5

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeterWeyl.ca.statement: theorem card_perm (n : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) = n.factorial

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.doc:
/-- Against `1/(1 + k²)` for the exponential damping: `∫ 2ε/(ε² + k²) · 1/(1 + k²) dk = 2π/(1 + ε)` (partial
fractions). -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.statement:
theorem damped_exp_lorentz (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε ≠ 1) :
    ∫ k : ℝ, 2 * ε / (ε ^ 2 + k ^ 2) * (1 / (1 + k ^ 2)) = 2 * π / (1 + ε)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphericalHar.statement: theorem cos_phi_int : ∫ p in (0 : ℝ)..(2 * π), Real.cos p = 0

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.doc: /-- The derivative of the sawtooth as a Fourier series: `1 - Σ_{|n| ≤ N} (-1)^n e^{inx} = 2 Σ_{n=1}^N (-1)^{n+1} cos nx`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.statement:
theorem comb_series (N : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    1 - ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) N, (-1 : ℂ) ^ n * Complex.exp (n * x * Complex.I) =
      ((2 * ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (n + 2) * Real.cos ((n + 1) * x) : ℝ) : ℂ)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphericalHar.statement: theorem sin_fifth_theta : ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..π, Real.sin t ^ 5 = 16 / 15

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.doc:
/-- `δ̂' = ik`: `-φ̂'(0) = ∫ i x φ(x) dx` (mathlib's derivative of the transform, in its normalisation:
`(𝓕 φ)'(0) = 𝓕(-2πi x φ)(0)`). -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.statement:
theorem delta_prime_hat (φ : ℝ → ℂ) (hφ : Integrable φ) (hxφ : Integrable fun x : ℝ => x • φ x) :
    deriv (𝓕 φ) 0 = 𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => (-2 * π * Complex.I * x) • φ x) 0

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TestFunction.doc: /-- `x^m e^{-x²/2}` is bounded for every `m`: the Gaussian is a Schwartz function. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TestFunction.statement: theorem gaussian_moment_bounded (m : ℕ) : ∃ C, ∀ x : ℝ, |x| ^ m * Real.exp (-x ^ 2 / 2) ≤ C

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Plancherel.p.doc: /-- The polarised form (mathlib): `⟪𝓕 f, 𝓕 g⟫ = ⟪f, g⟫`. -/

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeterWeyl.cl.statement:
theorem class_coeff_two :
    ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..π, 2 * t * (2 * π - 2 * t) * (1 + 2 * Real.cos (2 * t) + 2 * Real.cos (4 * t)) * (2 / π * Real.sin t ^ 2) =
      -5 / 18

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PrincipalVal.doc: /-- `PV ∫ dx/(x(x² + 1)) = 0`: the symmetric truncations cancel by oddness. -/

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Inversion.Ga.doc: /-- The tails of the regularising Gaussians vanish as `ε → 0`, as stated (tested, not proved): `∫_{|y| > δ} G_ε → 0`. -/

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TheTransform.doc: /-- `ĝ = C e^{-σ²k²/2}` (with `C = σ √(2π)`) satisfies the transformed equation `ĝ' = -σ² k ĝ`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TheTransform.statement:
theorem gaussian_transform_ode (C σ k : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun k : ℝ => C * Real.exp (-σ ^ 2 * k ^ 2 / 2)) k =
      -σ ^ 2 * k * (C * Real.exp (-σ ^ 2 * k ^ 2 / 2))

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.MatrixCoeffi.doc: /-- The closed form `d¹ = 1 + sin θ A + (1 - cos θ) A²` with `A = -iJ_y`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.MatrixCoeffi.statement:
theorem d1_closed_form (θ : ℝ) :
    (1 : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ) + Real.sin θ • !![0, -(Real.sqrt 2 / 2), 0; Real.sqrt 2 / 2, 0, -(Real.sqrt 2 / 2); 0, Real.sqrt 2 / 2, 0] +
      (1 - Real.cos θ) • (!![0, -(Real.sqrt 2 / 2), 0; Real.sqrt 2 / 2, 0, -(Real.sqrt 2 / 2); 0, Real.sqrt 2 / 2, 0] *
        !![0, -(Real.sqrt 2 / 2), 0; Real.sqrt 2 / 2, 0, -(Real.sqrt 2 / 2); 0, Real.sqrt 2 / 2, 0]) =
    !![(1 + Real.cos θ) / 2, -(Real.sqrt 2 / 2) * Real.sin θ, (1 - Real.cos θ) / 2;
       Real.sqrt 2 / 2 * Real.sin θ, Real.cos θ, -(Real.sqrt 2 / 2) * Real.sin θ;
       (1 - Real.cos θ) / 2, Real.sqrt 2 / 2 * Real.sin θ, (1 + Real.cos θ) / 2]

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeriodicFunc.doc: /-- `F(t) = ∫₀^{2π} f(x) g(x - t) dx` is `2π`-periodic in `t`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeriodicFunc.statement:
theorem shifted_product_periodic (f g : ℝ → ℝ) (hg : Function.Periodic g (2 * π)) (t : ℝ) :
    ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..2 * π, f x * g (x - (t + 2 * π)) = ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..2 * π, f x * g (x - t)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.doc: /-- Away from `0`, `u = -e^{∓x}/2` solves `u'' - u = 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.statement:
theorem green_homogeneous (s x : ℝ) (hs : s = 1 ∨ s = -1) :
    deriv (deriv fun x : ℝ => -1 / 2 * Real.exp (s * x)) x - -1 / 2 * Real.exp (s * x) = 0

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.FourierCoeff.doc: /-- The square wave's sine coefficient: `b_n = (2/π) ∫₀^π sin n x dx = 2 (1 - (-1)^n) / (π n)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.FourierCoeff.statement:
theorem square_wave_bn (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    2 / π * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π, Real.sin (n * x) = 2 * (1 - (-1) ^ n) / (π * n)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.MatrixCoeffi.doc:
/-- The spin-`1` commutation relations in the weight basis: `[J_z, J_+] = J_+`, `[J_z, J_-] = -J_-`,
`[J_+, J_-] = 2 J_z`. -/

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.doc: /-- Against `cos k`: `∫ √(π/ε) e^{-k²/4ε} cos k dk = 2π e^{-ε}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.statement:
theorem damped_constant_cos (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∫ k : ℝ, Real.sqrt (π / ε) * Real.exp (-k ^ 2 / (4 * ε)) * Real.cos k = 2 * π * Real.exp (-ε)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Convergence..doc:
/-- The Lebesgue constants grow like `log N`, as stated (tested, not proved): `∫_{-π}^{π} |D_N| ≥ (8/π) log N`,
so the functionals `f ↦ S_N f(0)` are unbounded on continuous functions. -/

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Plancherel.h.doc: /-- `e^{-x²/2}` and `x e^{-x²/2}` are orthogonal: `∫ x e^{-b x²} dx = 0` by oddness (`b = 1` for the pair). -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Plancherel.h.statement: theorem hermite_orthogonal (b : ℝ) : ∫ x : ℝ, x * Real.exp (-b * x ^ 2) = 0

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Inversion.Di.doc: /-- The Dirichlet integral `∫ sin(ck)/k dk = π sgn c`, as stated (tested, not proved: not in mathlib). -/

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Plancherel.p.doc: /-- Poisson summation (mathlib, period 1): `Σ f(x + n) = Σ 𝓕 f(n) e^{2πinx}` for Schwartz `f`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Plancherel.p.statement:
theorem poisson_summation (f : SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) (x : ℝ) :
    ∑' n : ℤ, f (x + n) = ∑' n : ℤ, 𝓕 f n * fourier n (x : UnitAddCircle)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.doc: /-- The Dirac comb is tempered: `Σ_n c/(1 + 4π²n²) < ∞`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Distribution.statement: theorem comb_tempered (c : ℝ) : Summable (fun n : ℤ => c * (1 / (1 + 4 * π ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)))

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Parseval.eve.doc: /-- The even terms contribute a quarter: `Σ a / (2k)² = a π² / 24`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Parseval.eve.statement: theorem even_sq_sum (a : ℝ) : HasSum (fun k : ℕ => a / (2 * k : ℝ) ^ 2) (a * π ^ 2 / 24)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PrincipalVal.doc:
/-- The Sokhotski-Plemelj limit `lim ∫ φ/(x - iε) = PV ∫ φ/x + iπ φ(0)`, as stated for `φ = e^{-x²}` (tested, not
proved): the imaginary part tends to `π φ(0) = π`. -/

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SeriesComput.doc:
/-- The tail of `Σ 1/(2k+1)²` from `k = M` is at most `1/(4M)`: the maximal error of `S_N` for the triangle wave
decreases like `1/N`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SeriesComput.statement:
theorem odd_tail_bound (M K : ℕ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) :
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range K, oddInvSq (M + k) ≤ 1 / (4 * (M : ℝ))

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphereLaplac.doc:
/-- `Δ cos² θ = 2 - 6 cos² θ`: `cos² θ` is not an eigenfunction; `cos² θ = 1/3 + (cos² θ - 1/3)` splits it into the
eigenvalues `0` and `-6`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphereLaplac.statement:
theorem lap_cos_sq (θ : ℝ) (hs : Real.sin θ ≠ 0) :
    deriv (fun t : ℝ => Real.sin t * deriv (fun t : ℝ => Real.cos t ^ 2) t) θ / Real.sin θ = 2 - 6 * Real.cos θ ^ 2

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.MatrixCoeffi.statement: theorem schur_half_value : 2 * π * (4 * π) / (16 * π ^ 2) * 1 = 1 / 2

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TheTransform.doc: /-- The two-sided exponential and its two half-line pieces. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TheTransform.statement:
theorem two_sided_pieces (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (k : ℝ) :
    IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ => (Real.exp (-a * |x|) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (-(k * x) * Complex.I)) (Set.Iic 0) ∧
    IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ => (Real.exp (-a * |x|) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (-(k * x) * Complex.I)) (Set.Ioi 0) ∧
    ∫ x : ℝ, (Real.exp (-a * |x|) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (-(k * x) * Complex.I) =
      1 / (a - k * Complex.I) + 1 / (a + k * Complex.I)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PrincipalVal.doc: /-- The symmetric form: `∫_{-c}^{-ε} φ/x + ∫_ε^c φ/x = ∫_ε^c (φ(x) - φ(-x))/x`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PrincipalVal.statement:
theorem pv_symmetric (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (ε c : ℝ) (h1 : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => φ x / x) volume ε c)
    (h2 : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => φ (-x) / x) volume ε c) :
    (∫ x in (-c)..(-ε), φ x / x) + ∫ x in ε..c, φ x / x = ∫ x in ε..c, (φ x - φ (-x)) / x

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TestFunction.doc: /-- A non-negative kernel of unit mass supported in `[-δ, δ]` moves `f` by at most `sup_{|y| ≤ δ} |f(x-y) - f(x)|`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TestFunction.statement:
theorem mollifier_approx (f φ : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Continuous f) (hφc : Continuous φ) (hpos : ∀ y, 0 ≤ φ y)
    (δ ε x : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hsupp : ∀ y, δ < |y| → φ y = 0) (hmass : ∫ y in (-δ)..δ, φ y = 1)
    (hε : ∀ y, |y| ≤ δ → |f (x - y) - f x| ≤ ε) :
    |(∫ y in (-δ)..δ, f (x - y) * φ y) - f x| ≤ ε

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.ConvolutionP.statement: theorem convolution_comm_lsmul (f g : ℝ → ℝ) : f ⋆[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ] g = g ⋆[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ] f

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeriodicFunc.statement: theorem cos_int_mul_periodic (n : ℤ) (x : ℝ) : Real.cos (n * (x + 2 * π)) = Real.cos (n * x)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphereLaplac.doc:
/-- `Θ_{22}(θ) = 3 * Real.sin θ ^ 2` solves the associated Legendre equation with `l = 2`, `m = 2`:
`sin θ (sin θ Θ')' - m² Θ = -l(l+1) sin² θ Θ`, so `Θ e^{imφ}` has `Δ = -6`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphereLaplac.statement:
theorem legendre_22 (θ : ℝ) :
    Real.sin θ * deriv (fun t : ℝ => Real.sin t * deriv (fun t : ℝ => 3 * Real.sin t ^ 2) t) θ - 4 * (3 * Real.sin θ ^ 2) +
      6 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 * (3 * Real.sin θ ^ 2) = 0

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeriodicFunc.doc: /-- `sin x + sin (√2 x)` has no period `T ≠ 0`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.PeriodicFunc.statement:
theorem sin_sqrt_two_not_periodic (T : ℝ)
    (hT : ∀ x, Real.sin (x + T) + Real.sin (Real.sqrt 2 * (x + T)) = Real.sin x + Real.sin (Real.sqrt 2 * x)) :
    T = 0

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphericalHar.doc: /-- The Condon-Shortley phase for `l = 1`: `Y_{1,-1} = (-1) conj(Y_{11})` with `Y_{1,±1} = ∓√(3/8π) sin θ e^{±iφ}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.SphericalHar.statement:
theorem condon_shortley (θ φ : ℝ) :
    (Real.sqrt (3 / (8 * π)) * Real.sin θ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (-(φ : ℂ) * Complex.I) =
      -(starRingEnd ℂ) (-(Real.sqrt (3 / (8 * π)) * Real.sin θ : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((φ : ℂ) * Complex.I))

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Uncertainty..doc: /-- The Gaussian solves the equality condition: `(e^{-cx²/2})' = -c x e^{-cx²/2}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.Uncertainty..statement:
theorem gaussian_equality_case (c x : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (-c * x ^ 2 / 2)) x = -c * x * Real.exp (-c * x ^ 2 / 2)

KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TheTransform.doc: /-- The two-sided exponential transforms to the Lorentzian: `∫ e^{-a|x|} e^{-ikx} dx = 2a / (a² + k²)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.FourierAnalysis.TheTransform.statement:
theorem exp_two_sided (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (k : ℝ) :
    ∫ x : ℝ, (Real.exp (-a * |x|) : ℂ) * Complex.exp (-(k * x) * Complex.I) = ((2 * a / (a ^ 2 + k ^ 2) : ℝ) : ℂ)

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.sphere_riemann_0_1_.statement:
theorem sphere_riemann_0_1_0_1 (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : Real.sin (x 0) ≠ 0) :
    riemann sphere 0 1 0 1 x = Real.sin (x 0) ^ 2

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.polar_invMetric.doc: /-- The inverse of the polar metric is `diag(1, 1/r²)` away from the origin. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.polar_invMetric.statement:
theorem polar_invMetric (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : x 0 ≠ 0) :
    (metricAt polar x)⁻¹ = !![1, 0; 0, 1 / x 0 ^ 2]

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.polar_christoffel_1.statement: theorem polar_christoffel_1_0_1 (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : x 0 ≠ 0) : christoffel polar 1 0 1 x = 1 / x 0

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.bracket_killingY_ki.statement:
theorem bracket_killingY_killingZ (k : Fin 2) (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : Real.sin (x 0) ≠ 0) :
    lieBracket killingY killingZ k x = -killingX k x

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.equator_geodesic.doc:
/-- On the equator `θ = π/2` the only Christoffel symbol in the geodesic equation of `φ = t` vanishes, so the
equator is a geodesic. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.equator_geodesic.statement: theorem equator_geodesic (t : ℝ) : christoffel sphere 0 1 1 ![Real.pi / 2, t] = 0

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.dZ_on_fields.doc: /-- `dZ(∂_φ) = 0` and `dZ(∂_θ) = −sin θ`: pairing the differential with the coordinate fields. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.dZ_on_fields.statement:
theorem dZ_on_fields (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, pd i heightZ x * dphi i x) = 0 ∧ (∑ i, pd i heightZ x * dtheta i x) = -Real.sin (x 0)

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.radPolar_lieMetric.doc: /-- `L_{r ∂_r} g = 2 g` for the polar metric: the dilation rescales the metric. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.radPolar_lieMetric.statement: theorem radPolar_lieMetric (i j : Fin 2) (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) : lieMetric polar radPolar i j x = 2 * polar i j x

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.inversion_inversion.doc: /-- The inversion is its own inverse away from the origin. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.inversion_inversion.statement: theorem inversion_inversion (u v : ℝ) (h : u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 ≠ 0) : inversion (inversion (u, v)) = (u, v)

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.su2Matrix_det.doc: /-- Its determinant is `|a|² + |b|²`, so the matrix is in `SU(2)` exactly when `(a, b)` lies on the three-sphere. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.su2Matrix_det.statement: theorem su2Matrix_det (a b : ℂ) : (su2Matrix a b).det = ((Complex.normSq a + Complex.normSq b : ℝ) : ℂ)

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.sphere_christoffel_.statement:
theorem sphere_christoffel_0_1_1 (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : Real.sin (x 0) ≠ 0) :
    christoffel sphere 0 1 1 x = -(Real.sin (x 0) * Real.cos (x 0))

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.killingX_lieMetric.doc: /-- The Lie derivative of the round metric along `K₁` vanishes on the chart domain. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.killingX_lieMetric.statement:
theorem killingX_lieMetric (i j : Fin 2) (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : Real.sin (x 0) ≠ 0) :
    lieMetric sphere killingX i j x = 0

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.dxPolar_parallel.doc: /-- `∇ ∂_x = 0` in polar coordinates: the components vary but the covariant derivative vanishes. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.dxPolar_parallel.statement: theorem dxPolar_parallel (i k : Fin 2) (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : x 0 ≠ 0) : covDeriv polar dxPolar i k x = 0

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.raise_dZ.doc: /-- Raising the index of `dZ = (−sin θ, 0)` with the round metric gives the gradient `−sin θ ∂_θ`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.raise_dZ.statement:
theorem raise_dZ (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : Real.sin (x 0) ≠ 0) :
    (invMetric sphere x).mulVec ![-Real.sin (x 0), 0] = ![-Real.sin (x 0), 0]

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.raise_lower.doc: /-- Lowering then raising returns the original components: `g⁻¹ (g v) = v` for the round metric. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.raise_lower.statement:
theorem raise_lower (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : Real.sin (x 0) ≠ 0) (v : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    (invMetric sphere x).mulVec ((metricAt sphere x).mulVec v) = v

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.extDeriv_hopfForm.doc: /-- `d(cos θ dφ)` has the `(θ, φ)` component `−sin θ`: it is minus the area form. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.extDeriv_hopfForm.statement: theorem extDeriv_hopfForm (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) : extDeriv hopfForm ![0, 1] x = -Real.sin (x 0)

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.rotPolar_lieMetric.doc: /-- `L_{∂_φ} g = 0` for the polar metric: the rotation is an isometry. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.rotPolar_lieMetric.statement: theorem rotPolar_lieMetric (i j : Fin 2) (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) : lieMetric polar rotPolar i j x = 0

KaluzaKlein.christoffel_symm.doc: /-- For a symmetric metric the Christoffel symbols are symmetric in the lower indices. -/
KaluzaKlein.christoffel_symm.statement:
theorem christoffel_symm {n : ℕ} (g : Fin n → Fin n → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ) (hg : ∀ i j, g i j = g j i)
    (k i j : Fin n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    christoffel g k i j x = christoffel g k j i x

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.su2_det.doc: /-- `det g = sin²θ / 64` on `SU(2)`: the Euler-angle chart degenerates at `θ ∈ {0, π}`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.su2_det.statement: theorem su2_det (x : Fin 3 → ℝ) : (metricAt su2 x).det = Real.sin (x 0) ^ 2 / 64

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.su2_christoffel_0_1.statement:
theorem su2_christoffel_0_1_2 (x : Fin 3 → ℝ) (h : Real.sin (x 0) ≠ 0) :
    christoffel su2 0 1 2 x = Real.sin (x 0) / 2

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.sphere_gram_det.doc: /-- The Gram determinant of the spherical chart is `sin²θ`: the chart is regular away from the poles. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.sphere_gram_det.statement:
theorem sphere_gram_det (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    (Matrix.of fun i j => gram sphereEmbed i j x).det = Real.sin (x 0) ^ 2

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.bracket_dtheta_sinD.statement:
theorem bracket_dtheta_sinDphi (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    lieBracket dtheta sinDphi 0 x = 0 ∧ lieBracket dtheta sinDphi 1 x = Real.cos (x 0)

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.dphi_u.doc: /-- `∂u/∂φ = −v`: the first component of `∂_φ` in the stereographic chart. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.dphi_u.statement: theorem dphi_u (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) : pd 1 stereoU x = -stereoV x

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.sphere_gram.doc: /-- The Gram matrix of the spherical chart is the round metric: `G = diag(1, sin²θ)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.sphere_gram.statement: theorem sphere_gram (i j : Fin 2) (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) : gram sphereEmbed i j x = sphere i j x

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.meridian_geodesic.doc: /-- Along a meridian `θ = t`, `φ = φ₀` the geodesic equation needs only `Γ^k_{θθ}`, which vanish. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.meridian_geodesic.statement:
theorem meridian_geodesic (t φ₀ : ℝ) (h : Real.sin t ≠ 0) :
    christoffel sphere 0 0 0 ![t, φ₀] = 0 ∧ christoffel sphere 1 0 0 ![t, φ₀] = 0

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.velocity_on_height.doc: /-- The velocity `∂_θ + 2 ∂_φ` applied to the height gives `−sin θ`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.velocity_on_height.statement: theorem velocity_on_height (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) : (∑ i, pd i heightZ x * (![1, 2] : Fin 2 → ℝ) i) = -Real.sin (x 0)

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.wedge_dtheta_dphi.doc: /-- `(dθ ∧ dφ)_{θφ} = 1` and `(dθ ∧ dφ)_{φθ} = −1`: the wedge product is antisymmetric. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.wedge_dtheta_dphi.statement:
theorem wedge_dtheta_dphi (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    wedge dtheta1 dphi1 ![0, 1] x = 1 ∧ wedge dtheta1 dphi1 ![1, 0] x = -1

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.su2_invMetric.doc: /-- The inverse metric of `SU(2)` in Euler angles, away from `θ ∈ {0, π}`. -/

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.dphi_v.doc: /-- `∂v/∂φ = u`: the second component of `∂_φ` in the stereographic chart. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.dphi_v.statement: theorem dphi_v (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) : pd 1 stereoV x = stereoU x

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.south_of_north.doc: /-- The south stereographic coordinates `(X, Y)/(1 + Z)` of the point `stereoInv u v` are the inversion of `(u, v)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.south_of_north.statement:
theorem south_of_north (u v : ℝ) (h : u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 ≠ 0) :
    ((stereoInv u v).1 / (1 + (stereoInv u v).2.2), (stereoInv u v).2.1 / (1 + (stereoInv u v).2.2)) =
      inversion (u, v)

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.bracket_dphi_gradZ.doc: /-- `[∂_φ, −sin θ ∂_θ] = 0`: the rotation field commutes with the gradient of the height. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.bracket_dphi_gradZ.statement: theorem bracket_dphi_gradZ (k : Fin 2) (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) : lieBracket dphi gradZ k x = 0

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.polar_christoffel_0.statement: theorem polar_christoffel_0_1_1 (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : x 0 ≠ 0) : christoffel polar 0 1 1 x = -x 0

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.sphere_scalarCurvat.doc: /-- The scalar curvature of the unit sphere is `2`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.sphere_scalarCurvat.statement: theorem sphere_scalarCurvature (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : Real.sin (x 0) ≠ 0) : scalarCurvature sphere x = 2

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.polar_det.doc: /-- `det g = r²` for the polar metric. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.polar_det.statement: theorem polar_det (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) : (metricAt polar x).det = x 0 ^ 2

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.su2_scalarCurvature.statement: theorem su2_scalarCurvature (x : Fin 3 → ℝ) (h : Real.sin (x 0) ≠ 0) : scalarCurvature su2 x = 6

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.sphere_invMetric.doc: /-- The inverse metric of the sphere: `diag(1, 1/sin²θ)`, away from the poles. -/
KaluzaKlein.Geometry.sphere_invMetric.statement:
theorem sphere_invMetric (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : Real.sin (x 0) ≠ 0) :
    invMetric sphere x = !![(1 : ℝ), 0; 0, 1 / Real.sin (x 0) ^ 2]

KaluzaKlein.Geometry.dZ_components.statement: theorem dZ_components (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) : pd 0 heightZ x = -Real.sin (x 0) ∧ pd 1 heightZ x = 0

KaluzaKlein.Groups.mod2_kernel.statement: theorem mod2_kernel : ∀ k : ZMod 6, mod2 k = 0 ↔ k = 0 ∨ k = 2 ∨ k = 4

KaluzaKlein.Groups.sign_kernel.doc: /-- The kernel of the sign is the alternating group. -/
KaluzaKlein.Groups.sign_kernel.statement: theorem sign_kernel (g : Perm (Fin 3)) : Perm.sign g = 1 ↔ g ∈ alternatingGroup (Fin 3)

KaluzaKlein.Groups.schur_vector.doc:
/-- Schur's lemma for the vector representation of `so(3)`: a matrix commuting with the three generators is a
scalar. The nine commutation equations are read off entry by entry. -/
KaluzaKlein.Groups.schur_vector.statement:
theorem schur_vector (X : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℚ) (h : ∀ a, X * L a = L a * X) :
    X = X 0 0 • (1 : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℚ)

KaluzaKlein.Groups.zmod6_cosets.doc: /-- The two cosets `0 + H` and `1 + H` partition `ZMod 6`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Groups.zmod6_cosets.statement:
theorem zmod6_cosets :
    (H6.image fun h => (0 : ZMod 6) + h) = {0, 2, 4} ∧ (H6.image fun h => (1 : ZMod 6) + h) = {1, 3, 5} ∧
      ({0, 2, 4} : Finset (ZMod 6)) ∪ {1, 3, 5} = Finset.univ

KaluzaKlein.Groups.s3_not_comm.doc: /-- `(0 1)(0 2) ≠ (0 2)(0 1)` in `S₃`: the symmetric group is not abelian. -/
KaluzaKlein.Groups.s3_not_comm.statement: theorem s3_not_comm : swap (0 : Fin 3) 1 * swap 0 2 ≠ swap 0 2 * swap 0 1

KaluzaKlein.Groups.lagrange_a3.doc: /-- The order of a subgroup divides the order of the group (Lagrange), instantiated for `A₃ ⊆ S₃`. -/

KaluzaKlein.Groups.sign_examples.doc: /-- The sign of a transposition is `-1` and of a three-cycle `+1`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Groups.sign_examples.statement: theorem sign_examples : Perm.sign (swap (0 : Fin 3) 1) = -1 ∧ Perm.sign (swap (0 : Fin 3) 1 * swap 1 2) = 1

KaluzaKlein.rotation_deriv.doc: /-- `R(t)` solves the one-parameter subgroup equation `dR/dt = L₂ R` entrywise, so it is `exp (t L₂)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.rotation_deriv.statement:
theorem rotation_deriv (t : ℝ) (i j : Fin 3) :
    deriv (fun s => rotation s i j) t = (L2R * rotation t) i j

KaluzaKlein.so3_structure.doc: /-- The structure constants of `so(3)` are `ε_{abc}`: `⁅L_a, L_b⁆ = Σ_c ε_{abc} L_c`. -/
KaluzaKlein.so3_structure.statement: theorem so3_structure (a b : Fin 3) : ⁅L a, L b⁆ = ∑ c, eps a b c • L c

KaluzaKlein.Representations.su3_branchin.doc: /-- The `su(2)` subalgebra `λ₁, λ₂, λ₃` commutes with `λ₈`: the triplet and the singlet have zero `u(1)` charge. -/

KaluzaKlein.su2_brackets.doc: /-- `⁅T₀, T₁⁆ = T₂`, `⁅T₁, T₂⁆ = T₀`, `⁅T₂, T₀⁆ = T₁`: the same structure constants as `so(3)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.su2_brackets.statement: theorem su2_brackets : ⁅T 0, T 1⁆ = T 2 ∧ ⁅T 1, T 2⁆ = T 0 ∧ ⁅T 2, T 0⁆ = T 1

KaluzaKlein.rotation_mul.doc: /-- Rotations compose by adding angles: `R(s) R(t) = R(s + t)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.rotation_mul.statement: theorem rotation_mul (s t : ℝ) : rotation s * rotation t = rotation (s + t)

KaluzaKlein.Representations.so4_splits_c.doc: /-- `J` and `K` commute: `[J_a, K_b] = 0` for all `a, b`, so `so(4) ≅ su(2) ⊕ su(2)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.Representations.so4_splits_c.statement: theorem so4_splits_commute (a b : Fin 3) : ⁅J a, K b⁆ = 0

KaluzaKlein.so4_coset_reductive.doc: /-- `[𝔯, 𝔨] ⊆ 𝔨`: `[M₀₁, M₀₃] = −M₁₃`, `[M₀₁, M₁₃] = M₀₃`, `[M₀₁, M₂₃] = 0` (the isotropy generator `M₀₁` rotates `𝔨`). -/
KaluzaKlein.so4_coset_reductive.statement:
theorem so4_coset_reductive :
    ⁅M4 0 1, M4 0 3⁆ = -M4 1 3 ∧ ⁅M4 0 1, M4 1 3⁆ = M4 0 3 ∧ ⁅M4 0 1, M4 2 3⁆ = 0

KaluzaKlein.Bundles.hopf_on_sphere.doc: /-- The Hopf map sends the unit three-sphere `|a|² + |b|² = 1` to the unit two-sphere. -/
KaluzaKlein.Bundles.hopf_on_sphere.statement:
theorem hopf_on_sphere (a b : ℂ) (h : Complex.normSq a + Complex.normSq b = 1) :
    (hopf a b).1 ^ 2 + (hopf a b).2.1 ^ 2 + (hopf a b).2.2 ^ 2 = 1

KaluzaKlein.coset_reductive.doc: /-- `[L₂, L₀] = L₁` and `[L₂, L₁] = −L₀`: the isotropy generator maps `𝔨` to itself (reductive). -/

KaluzaKlein.coset_symmetric.doc: /-- `[L₀, L₁] = L₂ ∈ 𝔯`: the coset is symmetric. -/

KaluzaKlein.Bundles.hopf_phase.doc: /-- The Hopf map is constant along the fibres: multiplying `a` and `b` by the same phase does not change it. -/
KaluzaKlein.Bundles.hopf_phase.statement:
theorem hopf_phase (a b : ℂ) (t : ℝ) :
    hopf (a * Complex.exp (t * Complex.I)) (b * Complex.exp (t * Complex.I)) = hopf a b

KaluzaKlein.rotation_fixes_pole.doc: /-- The rotations about the `Z`-axis fix the north pole `(0, 0, 1)`. -/

KaluzaKlein.rotation_preserves_norm.doc: /-- Rotations preserve the unit sphere: the image of a unit vector is a unit vector. -/
KaluzaKlein.rotation_preserves_norm.statement:
theorem rotation_preserves_norm (t : ℝ) (v : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    ((rotation t).mulVec v) ⬝ᵥ ((rotation t).mulVec v) = v ⬝ᵥ v

KaluzaKlein.coset_charge_plus.doc: /-- `E₊ = L₀ + i L₁` has charge `−i` under `ad L₂`: `[L₂, E₊] = −i E₊`. -/
KaluzaKlein.coset_charge_plus.statement: theorem coset_charge_plus : ⁅LC 2, LC 0 + Complex.I • LC 1⁆ = -Complex.I • (LC 0 + Complex.I • LC 1)

KaluzaKlein.coset_charge_minus.doc: /-- `E₋ = L₀ − i L₁` has charge `+i` under `ad L₂`: `[L₂, E₋] = i E₋`. -/
KaluzaKlein.coset_charge_minus.statement: theorem coset_charge_minus : ⁅LC 2, LC 0 - Complex.I • LC 1⁆ = Complex.I • (LC 0 - Complex.I • LC 1)

KaluzaKlein.su3_coset_charges_lambda3.doc:
/-- The isotropy charges under `λ₃`: `[λ₃, λ₁ + iλ₂] = 2(λ₁ + iλ₂)`, `[λ₃, λ₄ + iλ₅] = (λ₄ + iλ₅)`,
`[λ₃, λ₆ + iλ₇] = −(λ₆ + iλ₇)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.su3_coset_charges_lambda3.statement:
theorem su3_coset_charges_lambda3 :
    ⁅gellMann 2, gellMann 0 + Complex.I • gellMann 1⁆ = (2 : ℂ) • (gellMann 0 + Complex.I • gellMann 1) ∧
      ⁅gellMann 2, gellMann 3 + Complex.I • gellMann 4⁆ = gellMann 3 + Complex.I • gellMann 4 ∧
      ⁅gellMann 2, gellMann 5 + Complex.I • gellMann 6⁆ = -(gellMann 5 + Complex.I • gellMann 6)

KaluzaKlein.rotation_moves_equator.doc: /-- The rotation by `t` about the `Z`-axis moves `(1, 0, 0)` to `(cos t, sin t, 0)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.rotation_moves_equator.statement: theorem rotation_moves_equator (t : ℝ) : (rotation t).mulVec ![1, 0, 0] = ![Real.cos t, Real.sin t, 0]

KaluzaKlein.su3_coset_not_symmetric.doc: /-- `[λ₁, λ₄] = i λ₇ ∈ 𝔨`: `[𝔨, 𝔨] ⊄ 𝔯`, so `SU(3)/U(1)×U(1)` is not symmetric. -/

KaluzaKlein.su3_coset_charges_lambda8.doc:
/-- The isotropy charges under `λ₈`: `[λ₈, λ₁ + iλ₂] = 0`, `[λ₈, λ₄ + iλ₅] = √3 (λ₄ + iλ₅)`,
`[λ₈, λ₆ + iλ₇] = √3 (λ₆ + iλ₇)`. -/
KaluzaKlein.su3_coset_charges_lambda8.statement:
theorem su3_coset_charges_lambda8 :
    ⁅gellMann 7, gellMann 0 + Complex.I • gellMann 1⁆ = 0 ∧
      ⁅gellMann 7, gellMann 3 + Complex.I • gellMann 4⁆ = (Real.sqrt 3 : ℂ) • (gellMann 3 + Complex.I • gellMann 4) ∧
      ⁅gellMann 7, gellMann 5 + Complex.I • gellMann 6⁆ = (Real.sqrt 3 : ℂ) • (gellMann 5 + Complex.I • gellMann 6)

KaluzaKlein.so4_coset_symmetric.doc: /-- `[𝔨, 𝔨] ⊆ 𝔯`: `[M₀₃, M₁₃] = −M₀₁`, `[M₀₃, M₂₃] = −M₀₂`, `[M₁₃, M₂₃] = −M₁₂` (`S³` is a symmetric coset). -/

KaluzaKlein.Bundles.mobius_section_zero.doc:
/-- A continuous function on `[0, 2π]` with `s(2π) = −s(0)` vanishes somewhere: a section of the Möbius band,
which changes sign across the glued edge, has a zero. -/
KaluzaKlein.Bundles.mobius_section_zero.statement:
theorem mobius_section_zero (s : ℝ → ℝ) (hs : Continuous s) (h : s (2 * Real.pi) = -s 0) :
    ∃ x ∈ Set.Icc 0 (2 * Real.pi), s x = 0
